entry.content:
This fifth post in my series gives an overview of latest UX innovations in SAP Concur, for managing your travel and expense. The Joule Meeting Planning Agent is now even more powerful, able to flag big events taking place at locations which might spike hotel prices as well enabling you to block hotel rooms for attendees via the new Groupize integration. We are also introducing a number of powerful AI-assisted applications, such as the delegates dashboard or the approval manager, with AI embedded directly in the application – see for yourself!

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

The Concur UX innovations are covered in these sections:

Joule: Meeting planning agent enhanced
AI-assisted applications
-  Delegates dashboard
-  Approval manager
-  Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators
-  Outlook: Corporate card management
-  Expense reports
Further information

 

Joule: Meeting Planning Agent Enhanced

This is a great example of how we are shifting away from a “click through the UI” user experience towards an intent-based experience, where you state what you want and the system figures it out for you.

The recently introduced meeting planning agent is already very helpful when organizing a meeting with participants from various locations: it helps you to identify the best location and hotels to minimize travel costs and book the travel (for example flights) and hotels all in one go.

Figure 1 gives you an idea of what this looks like, when the user asks “I’m planning an offsite October 20th-24th, 3 people coming from Seattle, 2 from New York, and 2 from Miami. Find me an optimal location near an SAP office that minimizes travel for everyone”. As you can see, the response lists suitable office locations and recommends best options, and then asks whether you would like to proceed exploring flight and hotel options.

Figure 1: Meeting Planning Agent. Alt Text: Screeshot of Joule with user prompt at the top and response below, as described in the main text.

Watch this video to get a better idea of the user interaction of what is generally available already today:

  • Video: Meeting Planning Agent

As announced a few days ago, we are significantly enhancing its capabilities.

From a UX perspective,

  • we are enhancing the shift in interaction model towards natural language, intent-based experiences, and
  • we are integrating and consolidating, giving users the power of two products in one unified experience.

Intent-based: Imagine you are organizing a large meeting, with participants from many locations. Instead of clicking through location, date, and budget filters, you describe what you need in plain language – "somewhere with hotels near the office and good local food, avoiding conference weeks" – and Joule interprets that into a destination recommendation, proactively flagging conflicts (such as local events that would spike rates) that a filter-based search wouldn't surface on its own. For example, hotels in Munich are much more expensive during the Octoberfest weeks, as were those of Football (Soccer) World Cup venues when matches were scheduled there.

Integrated and consolidated: Especially for larger events, you want to block hotel rooms for attendees, to ensure that rooms are available for them, and also to get preferential rates. Up until now that meant going into a separate system, but we are integrating Groupize hotel room blocking functionality directly into Concur, so users can use Joule for this too. This reduces context-switching – one less system for planners to reconcile, and one continuous flow for the traveler from group booking to individual selection.

Figure 2 shows the start of a conversation covering this, where an RFP (request for proposal) is being created for sending to the proposed hotels.

Figure 2: Example Joule conversation for booking a block of hotel rooms leveraging integration with Groupize. Alt Text: Two screenshots showing a full-screen Joule conversation. The user prompted “I need a hotel block for GBTA Chicago”, and Joule makes a proposal for an RFP draft, with a buffer each side of the dates. The user specifies “Keep the buffer, 4 star, walking distance”, and Joule proposes three hotels, showing them on a map and providing cards for each with price per person. The user selected on, and Joule refines the RFP.

What changed for the end user:

  • Conversational input replaces structured search filters – plan a meeting the way you'd describe it to a colleague, not the way a form asks for it.
  • The system proactively surfaces risk (rate spikes, availability conflicts) instead of requiring the planner to know to check for it.
  • Attendees get a self-service booking link within the group's negotiated rate, removing a manual handoff step that used to sit with the event organizer.

What changed for the workflow:

  • Group accommodation data lives in one system of record instead of two, removing a reconciliation step planners used to own.
  • Built on an agent-to-agent model between Joule and Groupize — the products interact directly rather than the user bridging them manually.

This functionality is planned to become available to Early Adopter Care customers very soon (in September) and is planned to become generally available in Q4 this year.

Further reading

  • SAP Concur Sets New Standard for What AI Can Do for Travel and Finance Teams
  • The Business Travel Magazine: SAP Concur solution streamlines meeting planning 
  • Business Travel News Europe — Groupize meetings get handshake with Concur

 

AI-Assisted Applications

Nothing beats a good UI if you need a quick overview of what’s going on – that’s why people love dashboards. However, when you need to make decisions based on what you are looking at, that’s where AI can come in handy! Let’s have a look at some cool examples from the latest Concur release – many of which starting via Early Adopter Care (EAC) programs

  • AI-assisted delegates dashboard (EAC)
  • AI-assisted approval manager (EAC)
  • Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators (EAC)
  • AI-assisted corporate card management (EAC)
  • AI-assisted expense reports

AI-Assisted Delegates Dashboard (EAC)

This new dashboard helps assistants of executives and other travelers get their work done much more easily, by bringing together information from three different places all into one unified workspace, covering approvals, bookings and expenses. The dashboard also surfaces a prioritized "what needs your attention" view on login, rather than requiring the assistant to go looking across tools.

This is best explained by looking at some examples of what the design looks like. Figure 3 shows the Overview page, with the list of today’s tasks on the left, a row of cards across the top showing urgent tasks, ongoing trips, planning activities and follow-up activities, a map next to the list of ongoing trips, and at the bottom a list of recent activities.

Figure 3: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Overview tab. Alt Text: Image of the application as described in the main text.

Figure 4 shows the task view, with a row of cards across the top showing urgent tasks, ongoing trips, planning activities and follow-up activities above the overall list of tasks. To the right you see details for the selected task, related to a missing receipt, and how AI is recommending the next step.

Figure 4: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Task tab. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

Finally, Figure 5 shows an example of the travel view, showing large cards each representing an upcoming trip.

Figure 5: Design example of Delegates Dashboard, Travel tab. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

The AI-assisted delegates dashboard is available to Early Adopter Care customers now, with general availability planned for Q3/2026.

AI-Assisted Approval Manager (EAC)

With the help of AI, approving expense reports becomes much easier. The new AI-assisted approval manager gives you recommendations for each expense report that is pending your approval. The approval decision itself gets AI reasoning shown inline (why something's flagged as risk, what the spend trend looks like), so the reviewer isn't leaving the approval screen to go and build that context themselves.

Figure 6 shows an example, with three reports pending approval. AI recommends that you approve the first one, that you review the second one closely, with a bullet-point list of reasons why, and the third one recommends sending back to the requestor, again with a bullet-point list of reasons why. On the right you see a section with spend insights, with a chart showing planned vs actual team spend over time, above a list of approved reports, with indicators where AI helped with the approval.

Figure 6: AI-assisted approval manager. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

The AI-assisted approval manager is available to Early Adopter Care customers now, with general availability planned for Q4/2026.

Policy Optimizer and Benchmarking for Administrators (EAC)

The new control center for expense administrators, first released in June, has some exciting new AI-assisted features to optimizing travel policies and benchmarking program performance against similar organizations.

Policy optimization allows users to upload policy documents and AI will identify gaps between documented policies and what is set up in the system, helping them keep programs optimized and compliant.

Figure 7 shows the design of an example, where you see the “For You Today” section containing cards with recommended actions for you. On the right you see the AI recommendation, on the same screen, so that you have all the information you need surfaced in one place.

Figure 7: Policy optimizer and benchmarking for administrators in the control center for expense administrators. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

This new capability is available to customers via the Early Adopter Care program, with general availability currently planned for Q1/2027.

Outlook: AI-Assisted Corporate Card Management (EAC)

Planned to become available soon for Early Adopter Care, and generally available later this year, AI-assisted corporate card management will simplify virtual card administration by using AI to generate card programs from your policy documents, allow you to create auto-approval rules using natural language, and streamline employee virtual card requests. 

In the past, setting up a card program for your organization meant digging through lengthy policy documents, looking for spend limits, and manually configuring complex rules. Soon you will be able to simply upload your company’s travel and expense policy, and corporate card management will generate a virtual card program aligned to your policy. Spending limits are defined, merchant category codes are mapped, and a policy template is created for you. All you have to do is review.

We are also incorporating intent-based user experience into this: you will be able to use natural language to define auto-approval rules for corporate cards, in a similar manner to that provided by the Meeting Planning Agent described above. Auto-approval rules mean that employees can get funds faster and you can reduce the workload for approvers – providing an improved experience for everyone!

Figure 8 gives you an idea of the steps that are automated when creatinga new card program: it shows the pop-over displayed once you have triggered the creation. In the example shown, “Parsing Document Structure” and “Extracting Spending Limits” has been completed, “Mapping Merchant Categories” is in progress, and the subsequent steps are shown as “Matching Employees to Templates” and “Configuring Approval Workflows”.

Figure 8: Planned AI-assisted corporate card management. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

AI-Assisted Expense Reports

I don’t know anyone who actually enjoys compiling expense reports from the various receipts and invoices that they have. Now, Concur automates this tedious task for you.

Joule now assembles and audits expense reports automatically, from receipt to compliance check, so you go from tedious data entry to a quick review-and-submit.

Figures 9 and 10 show what this looks like: Figure 9 shows the pop-over you get when opening your expenses, informing you that Concur has automated your expense report, and offering you a “Go to Report” button. If you click on that, you’ll see the report as shown in Figure 10, with the “AI-assisted” link at the top. Clicking on that brings up the pop-over explaining “How this works”, listing the steps “Incoming expenses scanned”, “Related expenses added into report”, “Report details automatically populated”, and “You can review, modify, and submit”. It also explains “If something looks wrong” with an explanation that you can move expenses out, delete reports safely, since expenses will be moved to Available Expenses, and you can override fields that have been populated by our AI assistant.

Figure 9: AI-assisted expense report – pop-over indicating that Concur has automated your expense report. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

 

Figure 10: AI-assisted expense report with the pop-over explaining the AI-assistance. Alt Text: image of the application as described in the main text.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Expense Automation Agent – Capabilities and User Experience

 

Further Information

To get an overview of all the available Joule and AI capabilities with SAP Concur, look here:

  • Joule with SAP Concur solutions
  • Documentation: AI Features in SAP Concur

Further information about the latest SAP Concur release and announcements:

  • News: SAP Concur Sets New Standard for What AI Can Do for Travel and Finance Teams
  • Blog: SAP Concur Unveils New AI Innovations at GBTA 2026

  • SAP Concur page
  • SAP Concur road map

 

Continue Reading

  • SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 6: SAP LeanIX

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 6: SAP LeanIX
entry.content:
Co-author: Laura Lezeu

This sixth post in my series gives an overview of the latest UX innovations in SAP LeanIX, for managing your enterprise architecture. You’ll see how we are shifting to intent-based UX, where you state your intent rather than clicking around on screens, and how we are infusing AI into your applications to assist you in getting better outcomes, more easily and more quickly. Highlights are the Enterprise Architecture Assistant, the AI assistant for building custom reports, AI-guided actionable architecture recommendations, and AI-assisted automations and calculations. Our new MCP server gives agents access to LeanIX, and the AI Agent Hub makes it easy to govern every AI asset in your enterprise.

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

We’ve collected the UX innovations in these sections:

  • The shift in UX to intent-based UX, proactive insights, and workflow continuity
  • Answer your questions in seconds with the Enterprise Architecture Assistant
  • Create transformations utilizing the SAP LeanIX MCP Server
  • SAP AI Agent Hub: Govern every AI asset in your enterprise
  • Build custom reports with your AI assistant
  • AI-guided actionable Architecture Recommendations
  • Identify missing data on application fact sheets
  • Close the gap between architectural design and transformation execution
  • AI-Assisted Automations and Calculations: Create and troubleshoot faster

 

The Shift in UX to intent-based UX, proactive insights, and workflow continuity

Enterprise architecture has always evolved alongside the technologies it governs. The rise of AI is creating a different kind of pressure, not just a new asset class to manage, but a shift in what the discipline can do and who can participate in it. That is where our UX focus has been.

A thread running through this is the shift from expertise-dependent to intent-dependent access. Querying the workspace, building custom reports, configuring automations and calculations, these tasks no longer require technical skills or developer support. They require the ability to describe what you need.

A second thread is about where insight comes from. The workspace has historically been a tool you consult. We've been working on evolving the tool to surface these insights: flagging data quality gaps to the people who can fix them, highlighting improvement opportunities in the IT landscape, marking at-risk transformations before they become problems. The shift from reactive to proactive is gradual, but it is directional.

The third area is workflow continuity in target architecture planning. Designing a future state, connecting it to initiatives, and governing execution have until now involved manual bridging across steps and views. This release brings those into a single connected flow.

And cutting across all of it: the same discipline SAP LeanIX applies to application portfolios: inventory, lifecycle, governance, now extends to AI agents themselves. As organizations scale their AI deployments, that architectural layer is no longer optional.

 

Answer Your Questions in Seconds with the Enterprise Architecture Assistant

Getting answers about your architectural landscape has always involved too many steps: filter, export, cross-reference, repeat. The Enterprise Architecture Assistant in SAP LeanIX Enterprise Architecture Management removes that overhead.

Ask a question in plain language. Get a sourced answer in seconds.

Figure 1: Enterprise Architecture Assistant. Alt Text: two screenshots, the top one showing the start page of the EA Assistant, with three “Try asking” suggestions above the prompt input field. The bottom one shows the user has entered “Which applications are reaching end of life within the next 24 months”, followed by the anser in a two column table, listing four applications and their end-of-life date.

What it does for an Enterprise Architect:

  • Queries your inventory, connected Confluence pages, and workspace files in one go, without manual aggregation.
  • Understands your meta model, so results are contextually relevant, not just keyword matches.
  • Every answer is attributed to its source, so you can trace and trust what you're seeing.
  • Nothing changes in your workspace without your explicit approval.

What it means for the business:

  • Risk and lifecycle audits that used to take hours can be run as needed.
  • Data quality checks and rationalization analysis become ongoing, not periodic.
  • Faster architectural decisions with less analyst overhead.

Beyond querying, the assistant can do structural work: generate capability models, draft architecture decision records, and propose fact sheet updates based on a document you reference.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Enterprise Architecture Assistant

 

Create Transformations with the SAP LeanIX MCP Server

The SAP LeanIX MCP server connects AI agents directly to the workspace data, enabling them to act on the architectural landscape rather than just read about it.

Figure 2: MCP Server available in Transformations Explorer. Alt Text: screenshot of the Transformations Explorer, with “Model Context Protocol” annotation and arrow to the left of the screenshot, pointing to the menu entry “Custom Transformation” on the left side of the screenshot.

For end users:

  • AI agents can query your transformation and milestone data without manual exports or copy-paste workflows.
  • Upcoming write capabilities mean you can create transformations, initiatives, and milestones through an AI assistant directly.

For the business:

  • Reduces manual overhead for routine architectural updates.
  • Accelerates the path from insight to action in transformation planning.
  • Positions the workspace as an active participant in AI-driven workflows, not just a data store.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: MCP Server

 

SAP AI Agent Hub: Govern Every AI Asset in Your Enterprise

AI agents are being deployed faster than anyone can track them. The result is a fragmented landscape where no one has a clear picture of what's running, what it touches, or whether it's safe. The SAP AI Agent Hub is built to fix that.

Video 1: AI Agent Hub (click on the image to start the video).

What it does for AI Centre of Excellence teams:

  • Automatically discovers agents, LLMs, and MCP servers across SAP, Microsoft, Google, AWS, Databricks, and ServiceNow, no manual cataloguing.
  • Gives every asset a structured record: classification, status, architecture decisions, AI risk rating, and compliance mappings.
  • Provides a formal verification workflow so nothing stays ungoverned.
  • Surfaces observability data at session level: goal completion rate, tool-call correctness, execution paths, and root-cause analysis.
  • Maps agents to the business units, roles, and skills they affect, via SAP SuccessFactors integration.

What it means for the business:

  • Visibility into AI agent sprawl before it becomes a compliance or risk problem.
  • A defensible governance record for every AI asset in your landscape, regardless of who built it or where it runs.
  • Faster rationalization decisions: you can see what agents actually do, how they perform, and what they touch.

Find out more on the

  • Product page: SAP AI Agent Hub

 

Build Custom Reports with Your AI Assistant

Building a custom report used to mean a ticket, a wait, and a developer. That dependency is gone.

Connect the SAP LeanIX MCP server to your IDE, link your preferred AI assistant and describe what you need in plain language. The assistant generates the code. You preview it against your live workspace data, refine it through follow-up prompts, and publish directly to your workspace.

Figure 3: Example of a custom report built using natural language input. Alt Text: Screenshot of the “Reports” view, showing business capabilities per organizational unit, with columns of capabilities for Australia, Brazil, etc.

For end users:

  • No coding required: describe the report you need and iterate conversationally.
  • Results reflect your actual workspace structure: reports are fully aware of your meta model configuration.

For the business:

  • Custom reporting on demand, without queuing development work or waiting on a sprint cycle.
  • Teams get the specific view of architectural data they need, when they need it.
  • Any workspace user can create and publish reports, scaling access beyond a single team.

 

AI-Guided Actionable Architecture Recommendations

Analysing your IT landscape for improvement opportunities is ongoing work: identifying where to reduce technical debt, where costs can be optimized, where the biggest risks sit. We worked on a capability that surfaces that guidance directly, without requiring you to build the analysis from scratch each time.

Figure 4: AI architecture recommendations. Alt Text: Screenshot showing Inventory view, with a section on the left “Insight Details”, and a section on the right “Recommended Steps”, with the second step being “Generate a survey for app owners to verify compatibility”. This step has been triggered, shown via a text box with “Thinking” and a list of actions already done by AI along with the next one.

For end users:

  • AI-generated recommendations highlight key areas for improvement in the IT landscape, so you spend time acting on insights rather than constructing them.
  • Recommendations are grounded in the actual workspace data, specific to your architecture, not generic best practices.

For the business:

  • Continuous architectural guidance without dedicated analysis cycles.
  • Earlier identification of risk and inefficiency, tied to concrete improvement areas.
  • Moves the workspace from a record system toward an active advisor for architectural decision-making.

This is the first set of AI-generated insights for SAP LeanIX, with scope and sophistication expanding over the course of the year.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Architecture Guidance

 

Identify Missing Data on Application Fact Sheets

Incomplete application data is one of the most common sources of poor architectural decisions. We now surface data quality gaps directly in the inventory, so the people responsible for fixing them see them without needing to run a separate analysis.

Figure 5: Missing data highlighted in fact sheet. Alt Text: Screenshot of the Inventory view, with four cards highlighted at the top in a “Data Quality Insights” section, showing the number of applications not assigned to any Organizations, to any Business Capabilities, with missing Descriptions, and missing Lifecycle.

For end users:

  • Four cards highlight applications missing a description, lifecycle, organization relation, or business capability relation.
  • Selecting a card filters the inventory to the exact applications that need attention, no manual cross-referencing required.

For the business:

  • Data quality issues are surfaced to application owners proactively, rather than discovered during audits or reviews.
  • Improves the reliability of architectural decisions that depend on application data.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: Data Quality Insights

 

Close the Gap between Architectural Design and Transformation Execution

Planning a target architecture involves more steps than most tools support end to end. SAP LeanIX Architecture and Road Map Planning has been updated across the full journey: from designing the future state, to defining a plan, to governing its execution.

Design and Decide

You can now design your target architecture in a dedicated diagram type. Starting from your existing as-is architecture, you add transformations using any transformation template and model the future state of your architectural landscape. You can switch between viewing the current state, the changes, and the target state.

Once your design is ready, a guided experience lets you assign transformations to existing or new initiatives in one workflow. You can also generate an AI-assisted architecture decision from the diagram, including a structured description of the planned changes and a list of affected fact sheets.

Figure 6: Example target architecture diagram for finance capability. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a visual editor with a canvas in the middle showing a Finance box, containing an “Accounting & Billing” and “Audit/Assurance/Legal” box, each with a number of functional boxes therein. The “SAP FI” box within “Accounting & Billing” has three arrows pointing to boxes “Australia”, “France”, “Spain” outside the Finance box.

Plan

In the transformations explorer, transformations originating from diagrams are visually marked so you can trace their source, move them between initiatives, set milestones, jump back to the diagram, and navigate directly to the roadmap report.

Figure 7: Transformations Explorer example. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a table with Initiatives, with the filter “By Affected Fact Sheet” chosen.

Govern

Once your plan is in place, the roadmap report provides an overview to track execution. It now supports visual milestone editing alongside a range of usability improvements, including zoom controls, exact dates on the timeline, currency formatting, and adjustable column widths. In the roadmap and any other report, the side panel now shows all transformations impacting a fact sheet, so you can review, execute, or edit them without leaving the report. The landscape report with the impact view shows which applications and IT components are affected by active initiatives and highlights at-risk transformations.

This is the first release of these target architecture planning capabilities, and we will continue building them out throughout 2026.

Figure 8: Example initiative roadmap. Alt Text: Screenshot of the top part of the Reports view screen, showing a roadmap in a Gantt chart visualization, with a parent entry “Cloud Transformation 2027” and Wave 1 and Wave 2 child entries.

 

AI-Assisted Automations and Calculations: Create and Troubleshoot Faster

Workspace admins who set up automations to keep data current or calculations to roll up metrics can now do both faster and with more visibility into what is running.

AI-Assisted Automations

Describe your workflow in plain English and get a fully configured automation, including triggers, conditions, and actions, ready to activate. The generated automation references your workspace meta model, so triggers and conditions use your actual fact sheet types, fields, and subscription roles. Every result is editable before you go live. For example: "When the lifecycle phase of an application fact sheet changes to End of Life, send an email to all subscribers."

When an automation fails, you now see exactly which action failed and why. The execution log shows the full run history and can be filtered by status, date, automation name, and fact sheet, plus a per-action timeline for every run.

Figure 9: AI-assisted automations. Alt Text: Screenshot of the Automations configuration screen, showing an entry “Tag Gold on Perfect Functional Suitability” showing a trigger and action for this. At the bottom an “Ask AI” field is shown with a prompt entry field containing the text “When functional fit is set to perfect on an application, add the tag Gold”. Below that the text “Steps generated. AI can make mistakes – review results”.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Automations

Calculations

Previously, configuring calculations required writing JavaScript. Now you can describe the metric or field logic you need and get a ready-to-run formula that accounts for your workspace's fact sheet types, fields, and relations. The generated code includes inline comments so you can verify the logic before activating. For example: "For business capability fact sheets, sum total cost of ownership across related applications that are in the active lifecycle phase."

The enhanced configurations for automations and calculations are part of base AI capabilities. They require signed AI terms and the activation of base AI capabilities, but not AI credits. The execution logs for automations and calculations are available in all workspaces.

Figure 10: AI-assisted calculations. Alt Text: Screenshot of a calculation Editing “Total cost of ownership”, with fields for Details and Target Field. At the bottom an “Code Generation with AI” field is shown with a prompt entry field containing the text “For business capability fact sheets, sum total cost of ownership across related applications that are in the active lifecycle phase”.

Find out more:

  • Documentation: AI-Assisted Calculations

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 7: SAP Analytics Cloud
entry.content:
This seventh post in my series gives an overview of latest UX innovations in SAP Analytics Cloud. We have many enhancements for Story design and usage, for example the new Data Panel and drag & drop capabilities, three new chart types, AI-assisted prompt insights, and more. We have also enhanced simulations with Compass, introduce My Metrics notifications with Microsoft Teams, improved search and filter, as well as significant improvements in working with tables, amongst others.

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

I’ve collected the UX innovations in these sections:

  • Story design and usage (7 innovations!)
  • Simulation enhancements via Compass updates (2 innovations)
  • Microsoft Teams for My Metrics notifications
  • Redesigned search and filter experience
  • Tables enhancements (2 innovations)
  • New blog card on home screen

 

Story Design and Usage

Creating and using stories becomes much easier now, with some major enhancements as well as many improvements in details:

  • New Data Panel for adding and working with your data models.
  • Recent and favorites in open and save dialogs.
  • 3 new chart types: Sankey, Gauge, Funnel.
  • Composite Versioning.
  • AI-assisted prompt insights.
  • AI-assisted story code generation for story scripts.
  • New look with the Horizon visual theme.
  • Data filter parameters for more intuitive filtering.

New Data Panel for Adding and Working with Your Data Models

The new data panel further optimizes the experience of creating stories by improving overall usability. It starts right at the beginning, when you want to create a story by adding a data model. It used to be difficult to figure out how to do that, but now when you create a new story, the Data Panel comes up immediately, showing you the options of adding from an existing model or dataset, from a data source, or from a file. See Figure 1 for an example.

Figure 1: New Data Panel for adding data to a story. Alt Text: Screenshot of UI for creating a new story, with the Data Panel shown on the right with three cards for adding data, as described in the main text.

Recent and favorites: When adding a data model you can now choose from your recent or favorites, which can dramatically reduce the number of clicks needed.

Central overview of data: once you have added a data model, the Data Panel becomes the central reference point for understanding and working with your data, where you can explore the full structure of the model, i.e. primary and secondary structure, dimensions, and location dimensions.

  • For consumers: This makes it significantly easier for consumers of the story to understand the overall structure of the data models as they build additional visualizations, without leaving the story canvas.

For consumers – continuous exploration across data models: Consumers can now add additional data models directly within the Data Panel, and as each new model is added it is surfaced immediately, making it easier to navigate across multiple data models within the same story.

For complex dashboards, the Data Panel goes even further. As a consumer selects a specific visualization on the canvas, the Data Panel dynamically updates to reflect the data model associated with that visualization. If the consumer clicks away, the panel retains the last used data model, ready for the next visualization to be created.

Figure 2: Data Panel showing details of data model and supporting drag and drop. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a story, with the Data Panel opened and next to it the Builder panel. The “Headcount” measure is being dragged into a card on the story page.

More usability improvements: we have addressed several requests raised by customers:

  • Decoupled from the Builder Panel, which is still available as a manual configuration tool
  • Toggle between Description, ID, and ID & Description in the Data Panel, so you decided how entities are displayed
  • Powerful search with number of entities preview

Drag & Drop for Charts: Consumers Can Build Visualizations Naturally

Create charts: with the Data Panel now visible alongside their story canvas, we let consumers create charts using drag and drop: you can now drag from the Data Panel directly onto a Chart Widget on the canvas.

Updating existing visualizations: until now changing the data model on an existing visualization was a multi-click process. Now, consumers can simply drag a field from a different model in the Data Panel directly onto an existing chart: the visualization updates dynamically to the new data model, as you can see in Figure 3.

Figure 3: Drag and drop for charts from Data Panel. Alt Text: an animation showing an “Expense” measure being dragged into a chart showing Gross Margin per Location, which is then automatically updated.

Find out more about the Data Panel and drag and drop:

  • Improved Data Access in Stories: Introducing the Data Panel and Drag & Drop Creation of Charts

Recent and Favorites in Open and Save Dialogs

You can now access Recent and Favorites directly within file open/save dialogs. These tabs allow quick access to recently used or starred stories, models, and folders, saving you time navigating through the file repository hierarchy. This is particularly helpful if you as a consumer work repeatedly with the same datasets.

 It gives you:

  • Recent View: Displays a list of files recently accessed (created, edited, or opened).
  • Favorites View: Shows folders or files you have marked as a favorite, facilitating faster access.
  • Save Dialogs: Enables saving items directly into designated Favorite folders.

Figure 4 shows an example from the Data Panel, where you can select an existing dataset or model.

Figure 4: Favorites and Recent entities offered when selecting. Alt Text: Screenshot showing a “Select Dataset or Model” pop-over, with the two Views “Favorites” and “Recent” highlighted on the left.

Three New Chart Types

These three new chart types give you additional visualization options: Funnel, Gauge, and Sankey.

Funnel Chart

Funnel charts are used to visualize stage-by-stage drop-off, be that for a sales pipeline, conversion funnel, or any multi-step process with attrition at each stage.

Figure 5 shows an example for an IT sales pipeline, showing how leads starting at 100% reduce to 62% in status “Qualification”, 43% in “Proposal”, 31% in “Negotiation”, and finally 25% “Closed Won”. On the right you see how the chart gives you more details when you mouse-over a segment, in this case the segment “Proposal”, with the pop-over showing the percentage conversion rate of the leads entering the stage (69% of those in “Qualification” end up as “Proposal”).

Figure 5: Funnel chart example. Alt Text: Two screenshots next to each other of a funnel chart as described in the main text. The image on the right shows the pop-over.

Gauge Chart

Gauge charts provide a compact, at-a-glance way to track a KPI's progress against a target or threshold, popular for dashboard summary tiles.

Figure 6 shows three examples:

  • A threshold, showing the default thickness and default 180 degree angle with a needle representing a concrete data point.
  • A measure comparison with small angle and thickness.
  • A version comparison with large angle and thickness.

Figure 6: Gauge chart example. Alt Text: Screenshot showing three gauge charts in a row, as described in the text.

Sankey Chart

Sankey charts help you visualize how a value or a quantity grows or declines through a series of stages in a process.

A Sankey chart is a flow diagram in which the width of each connecting band is proportional to the weight it represents. It is the natural choice whenever an analyst needs to show how a measure — revenue, headcount, energy consumption, or any other quantity — is distributed, transformed, or lost as it moves through a series of stages. The Sankey chart makes the relative magnitude of each flow immediately visible, allowing viewers to identify the largest contributors and the most significant losses at a glance, without needing to read individual data labels.

Figure 7 shows two examples:

  1. Account hierarchy: the example shows the various contributing factors in an income statement, starting with overall net income, and then going through stages where taxes and other income and expenses are shown as bands reducing operating income, then bands for operating expenses and other operating revenue reducing gross margin, before finally showing the band for cost of goods sold reducing the net revenue.
  2. Multi-dimension and measure flow: a general-purpose flow chart that can have multiple dimensions as stages and a single measure as the flow quantity. The example has the cost as the quantity between various stages of assembly line in a Bill of Material (BOM) flow. It shows how the cost breaks down from finished vehicle on the left through stages “major assembly”, “sub-assembly”, “component” and “raw material / part”.

Figure 7: Sankey chart examples. Alt Text: Screenshot showing two charts, #1 above #2, as described in the main text.

Find out more about these three new chart types:

  • Three New Chart Types in SAP Analytics Cloud: Sankey, Gauge, and Funnel

Composite Versioning

As a composite designer you can now manage up to 10 versions of a composite, one of which is the active version. You can restore or revert to previous versions through the version history whenever needed.

This new feature reduces disruption for story viewers by allowing quick recovery to a stable version of a composite and improves reliability and safety when updating composite artifacts.

Figure 8: Composite versioning. Alt Text: Screenshot showing the composite view, with a side-panel “File Versions” on the right, showing four cards, with the current version details (Restored From “Version 4”, Changed By, Changed On) at the top. Below that cards for Versions 6, 5 and 4, each with a section “Changes Made”.

AI-Assisted Prompt Insights

Story designers can now add AI-assisted prompt insight widgets that combine a customizable prompt with data from a table or chart, and send that context directly to the Large Language Models. This enriches dashboards for planning and analytics scenarios, supporting structured analysis, risk assessment, and other insight-driven workflows. Figure 9 shows what this looks like for a consumer.

Figure 9: An example of AI-assisted prompt insights shown in a story. Alt Text: Screenshot of a scenario simulation, with two AI prompt insights in a panel on the right, each with multiple paragraphs of text.

AI-Assisted Story Code Generation for Generating Story Scripts

This brings generative AI into story scripting itself: describe what you want in natural language and get working script logic back, or ask AI to explain an existing script in plain terms. A genuine time-saver for designers who aren't full-time scripting experts

See it in action and have a look at this in more detail:

  • Video: AI-Assisted Story Code Generation for SAP Analytics Cloud
  • Blog post: AI-Assisted Story Code Generation for SAP Analytics Cloud

New Look with the Horizon Visual Theme

New stories in SAP Analytics Cloud get the new, improved visual theme based on the Horizon visual theme of SAP Fiori. As a result, new stories look modern and consistent with other products from SAP. No additional configuration is required.

Some of the notable changes are updated chart color palettes, new button colors and new font colors across widgets. Figure 10 show a sample of what this can look like in a story:

Figure 10: Example of new story default theme. Alt Text: A screenshot sowing a bar chart, a line chart and a table with a two bar charts with the new look.

Users continue to have the option to select which theme they want to use, and you can continue to use the widget style panel to override it. Also, custom brand themes can still be applied as before.

Find out more in this series of blog posts:

  1. New Stories, New Look: The Default Story Theme Is Getting an Update
  2. Replacement of the pre-delivered story theme to align with SAP Morning Horizon
  3. New Administration Setting - Define a story theme as the default at the tenant level

 

Data Filter Parameters for More Intuitive Filtering

Users can now filter data much more intuitively, for example, by defining certain entries or ranges to exclude, or by being able to simply say “from last week” or “yesterday”. As time progresses, the actual week or day covered by “last week” or “yesterday” changes. We call these latter filters “dynamic date ranges”.

This is made possible by the new data filter parameters, which makes the way data actions use parameter values more flexible, consistent, and aligned with the way users work in stories. Data filter parameters help to reconcile what the user selects and visualizes (including dynamic filter selections) with what the data action processes.

It represents a new parameter type that allows any number of dimension filters to be passed as-is into a single parameter, while allowing the filter selection to cover to dynamic story filters and input controls, including support for:

  • Exclusions (“everything except…”)
  • Dynamic date ranges or custom current date selections
  • Attribute based dimension filters

This means that you could for example pass the two dynamic date range dimension filters “last week” and “this week” to the single “posting date” filter parameter. Figure 11 shows an example for defining a date range.

Figure 11: Example data filter parameter for data actions – defining a date range. Alt Text: Screenshot of the top part of a story, where the user can define a date range for the year, with a “Look Back” field containing 1, and a “Look ahead” field containing 0.

 

Simulations Enhancements via Compass Updates

Story Widget for Simulation Results

Planning and decision-making rely on having the right insights at the right time. Until now, you couldn’t embed simulation results directly into SAP Analytic Cloud stories. Now, you can, with the story widget for simulation results.

Simulation output is no longer confined to a standalone Compass view. The new story widget lets you drop simulation results directly into a regular SAC story, right alongside your other KPIs and visuals — ideal for executive-facing dashboards that blend actuals, forecasts, and scenarios in one place.

Figure 12: Compass widget for embedding simulations in stories. Alt Text: Screenshot of a story for Budget Review showing three widgets next to each other: a table, the new compass widget, and a widget for Risk Scenarios.

Find out more here:

  • Introducing the Compass Widget: Bringing Risk Context Into Your Stories

Smart Boundaries

Smart Boundaries’ predictive range proposals take the guesswork out of setting up a scenario driver. Instead of manually entering upper and lower bounds for a driver's uncertainty range, Smart Boundaries proposes a sensible range for you automatically, based on analysis of the historical data, without the hassle of technical setup.

Find out more:

  • Compass: Predictive Range Proposal "Smart Boundaries"

 

Microsoft Teams for My Metrics Notifications

You can now receive your My Metrics report notifications directly with Microsoft Teams. If you spend a lot of time in Teams, this will save you from having to switch to other applications to access critical metric updates, and will help you to act on them quickly.

The other existing notification channels, the Notification Center in SAP Analytics Cloud and email inbox, continue to be supported. The Microsoft Teams delivery channel is fully consistent with these two existing channels. The notification content includes all standard report details: Metrics List Name, Subscription Name, Recurrence Pattern, Start Date, End Date, an Overview of Metrics table with Latest Value, Changes in Value, Previous Value, and Latest Variance — plus clickable metric name links and a direct 'Open My Metrics' deep-link to SAP Analytics Cloud. Figure 13 shows an example.

Figure 13: Example My Metrics report posted in a Microsoft Teams chat. Alt Text: Screenshotof a Microsoft Teams chat with a detailed My Metrics report showing text and a table with hyperlinks.

Find out more here:

  • Microsoft Teams as a Delivery Channel for My Metrics Reports in SAP Analytics Cloud

 

Redesigned Search and Filter Experience

Searching and filtering within stories, pages and widgets become much more intuitive now.

When filtering in SAP Analytics Cloud, you're usually doing one of two things:

  • quickly finding a set of members and applying them immediately or
  • refining your selection step by step before committing.

The redesigned search experience in the Q3 2026 release makes both easier. For starters, when you enter a search term, it automatically deselects “All” – the previous selection is no longer in the way. During an active search, the “Apply Selection” button discards the previous selected members and replaces them with the current search result directly.

New Replace and Update actions help you make a more complex selection by allowing you to run consecutive searches to build up your final results list before committing:

  • Replace starts fresh: the current selection is completely discarded and replaced with the search result. Members that were previously selected but are not in the search results will be removed.
  • Update adds to what you have: Search results are merged into the existing selection. Previously selected members are kept, and any search results are added on top. Any deselections made during the search are also applied.
  • “Apply Selection" commits the draft and closes the search.

Figure 14 shows the new options in the filter panel on the left.

Figure 14: new search and filter options “Replace” and “Update”. Alt Text: Screenshot of a story with a side panel on the left for Filters, showing the search text entry field above a “Replace” and “Update” button.

Look at this blog post for more information, including two animated GIFs showing it in action:

  • SAP Business Data Cloud - New Search and Replace actions in filter token

 

Tables Enhancements

Working with tables also becomes much easier now, with these enhancements:

  • Asymmetric reporting
  • Totals displayed for models with multiple data sources

Asymmetric Reporting

Asymmetric Reporting introduces a new way to design tables in SAP Analytics Cloud, enabling greater flexibility in how data is structured and presented within a single table.

Instead of relying on a strictly uniform layout, where all rows and columns follow the same dimensions, hierarchy, and granularity, Asymmetric Reporting enables selected aspects of a table layout to vary across different sections of the same table. Here are two examples:

  1. The first six columns could each represent a month, but the next two columns each represent a quarter, and the last column represent the next year.
  2. A table could have columns containing different types of data: for example, a table showing the 12 months of the year could have the first columns showing actuals up to the current month, the remaining month columns showing forecast data (coming from a different source), plus a column for full-year actuals plus forecast, merging data from both sources.

Each column represents a different perspective, with its own logic and level of detail, which is what makes the table asymmetric. Figure 15 shows an example similar to (2) above.

Figure 15: Example of an asymmetric table with columns containing different types of data. Alt Text: Screenshot showing an example asymmetric table as described under (2) in the main text.

Find out more here, and watch it in action:

  • Asymmetric Reporting Layout
  • Video: Asymmetric Reporting in SAP Analytics Cloud (6:42 min.)

Totals displayed for models with multiple data sources

Many organizations run their analytics across more than one data source. Actuals may come from one system, budgets from another. A single report often needs to bring these together in one place.

Until now totals were not available for tables in SAP Analytics Cloud that combined data from blended models. The aggregated row - the one that gives a report its summary, its bottom line - was simply missing. Users had to work around it, accept incomplete views, or maintain separate reports.

This gap is now closed. Tables and charts built on blended data models can now display totals. These totals update dynamically as filters are applied, so the summary row always reflects the current view of the data.

Find out more about this, as well as the improvement allowing business users to adapt the hierarchy level displayed in hierarchical tables:

  • Table Widget Improvements in SAP Analytics Cloud 2026 Q2 QRC

 

New Blog Card on Home Screen

To help you stay up to date with the latest blog posts about SAP Analytics Cloud in the SAP Community, such as this one, you now have the option to include the new Blog Card on your home screen. It shows the ten most recent blog posts about SAP Analytics Cloud from the SAP Community. Each entry shows the title, author, publish date, and a teaser. Click any post to open the full article in a new tab.

Figure 16 shows an example, and also shows how you can pin a blog post so that it stays at the top of the card.

Figure 16: New blog card on home screen. Alt Text: Two screenshots, on the left a home screen with the new card highlighted with a red border and an arrow pointing to the right screenshot, showing an enlarged blog card listing 3 posts, showing title, author, publish date, and teaser.

Find out more in this blog post:

  • What's New on the SAP Analytics Cloud Home Screen — Q2 2026 QRC: The New Blog Card

 

Further Information

Further information about the latest SAP Analytics Cloud releases:

  • Sneak Peek in to SAP Analytics Cloud release for Q2 2026
  • Video: SAP Analytics Cloud: Top 5 New Features – Q2 2026 Release Highlights (11:17 min.)
  • Sneak Peek in to SAP Analytics Cloud release for Q3 2026
  • Video: SAP Analytics Cloud: Top 5 New Features –  Q3 2026 Release Highlights (11.29 min.)
  • Documentation: What’s New in SAP Analytics Cloud

You can find general information about SAP Analytics Cloud here:

  • SAP Analytics Cloud product page.
  • SAP Community: SAP Analytics Cloud topic page
  • Roadmap: SAP Analytics Cloud
  • Documentation (SAP help portal): SAP Analytics Cloud Help

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 8: SAP Signavio
entry.content:
Co-authors: Sebastian Kaim, Steven Brueningk, Remy Saint Cricq, Shilpa Vadakkayil Payyanadan, Zahra Hajialibeigi, Charne Pearson, Yenny Lee

This eighth post in my series gives an overview of latest UX innovations in SAP Signavio, making its Process Transformation Suite more connected, more guided, and easier to understand. The Process Consulting Agent, Personalized Home Page and Unified Navigation & Unified Process Analysis and Mining are available now. We also have two great new AI capabilities for beta testing: the new AI-powered Process Modeler, and Company Memory to scale AI agents. Let’s have a look!

In case you missed it, Part 1 of this series provides general updates about Joule, SAP Work Zone and SAP Mobile Start.

 

Introduction

SAP Signavio is entering a new phase of user experience: clearer to navigate, simpler to use, and ready for the AI era. Across five key innovations the suite is becoming more connected, more guided, and easier to understand. Together, these updates reduce complexity across the full transformation journey and help users move more naturally from orientation to insight, from insight to action, and from individual process knowledge to AI-ready enterprise context.

This matters because the way people interact with enterprise software is changing. Users increasingly expect intelligent, guided, and flexible experiences that meet them where they are, whether through classic interfaces, embedded guidance, conversational assistance, or future agent-based workflows. A simpler and more predictable SAP Signavio is the foundation for that shift: when navigation, context, and core capabilities are easier to understand, both users and AI-enabled experiences can operate with greater clarity, trust, and continuity across the suite.

In this article, we highlight the key UX innovations from Q2 and Q3 that move SAP Signavio toward this future: a clearer structure, a more personal starting point, unified access to capabilities, and a stronger foundation for AI-assisted transformation work across the SAP Signavio Suite.

  1. Process Consulting Agent
  2. New Personalized Home Page and Unified Navigation
  3. Unified Process Analysis and Mining
  4. Company Memory & Atoms
  5. AI-Powered New Signavio Process Modeler

1. Process Consulting Agent

Process analysis and mining can unlock powerful insights, but interpreting and acting on them has traditionally required specialist expertise. The Process Consulting Agent makes these insights more accessible by enabling users to explore their processes through natural-language conversation.

Figure 1: Process Consulting Agent. Alt Text: Screenshot of the start screen, showing the text “Process Consulting Agent” above “Explore your process performance, in plain language”, above a prompt entry field. Below that there are 5 pre-defined prompts as clickable buttons, such as “What can you do for me” and “What are top value drivers”.

Powered by a multi-agent system, it retrieves and reasons over process data, runs relevant analyses, synthesizes findings, and recommends next steps. Users can simply ask questions such as “Are there inefficiencies in my order-to-cash process?” and receive contextual answers grounded in process data and industry best practices.

The experience brings insights, metrics, recommendations in one conversational flow. Users can move seamlessly from a question to an insight, explore the underlying details, and decide what to do next, without losing the context of the conversation.

The result is faster time to insight, less manual effort, and process analysis that can be used by everyone: from business users to experienced analysts, while keeping the user in control of the next step.

Find out more:

  • Process Consulting Agent: Process Insights, Reasoning and Recommendations One Conversation Away

 

2. New Personalized Home Page and Unified Navigation

Unified Navigation and Autonomous Suite Consistency

The redesigned SAP Signavio experience makes it easier for users to find what they need, stay oriented, and move through their work with less friction. Instead of switching between disconnected menus or relying on bookmarks, users now have one consistent left-side navigation that brings all SAP Signavio capabilities together in a single place. This gives people a clearer sense of where they are, what is available, and how each capability fits into the broader transformation journey.

This left-side navigation is a feature we have standardized across SAP’s product in the SAP Autonomous Suite, improving consistency for users of multiple products. Another feature introduced by Signavio is the shell bar, with the standardized icons on the top right. Figure 2 highlights the new navigation menu and the icons.

Figure 2: New left-side navigation and shell bar. Alt Text: Screenshot of the home page of a fictitious company “Acme” showing an image of their Customer & Operations Lifecycle. On the left the side-navigation shows a list of menu items. At the top right the icons in the shell bar are highlighted.

New Personalized Home Page

The new personalized home page, My Page, strengthens this sense of clarity by giving users a dedicated starting point for their daily work. With Favorites, Recently Visited items, and Quick Links, users can tailor the home page around the assets and destinations that matter most to them. The ability to rearrange widgets means the experience can adapt to different roles, priorities, and working styles, helping users get started faster and return to important work with fewer clicks.

Figure 3: New personalized “My Page” home page. Alt Text: Screenshot showing “Home” selected in the left-side navigation, and the main page showing the “My Page” tab selected, with three list cards displayed: Favorites, Recently Viewed and Quick Links.

Overall, the update shifts SAP Signavio toward a simpler, more personalized, and more predictable user experience. For end users, this means less time spent searching for tools and more time focused on process work, collaboration, and value realization across the suite.

 

3. Unified Process Analysis and Mining

Unified Process Analysis and Mining represents a landmark evolution in SAP's process transformation portfolio, unifying two previously distinct capabilities - SAP Signavio Process Insights and SAP Signavio Process Intelligence, into a single, cohesive analysis experience. This addresses a long-standing gap between fast, business-user-friendly diagnostics and deep, analyst-grade process mining. The result is a product that meets organisations wherever they are on their process maturity journey, without requiring them to switch tools as their needs grow.

At the heart of the combined offering is the speed-to-insight layer that originated in Process Insights: a rich library of SAP-defined business content that includes prebuilt KPIs, standardised process flows, industry benchmarks, and improvement recommendations. This gives business teams immediate, out-of-the-box visibility into core SAP processes such as procure-to-pay and order-to-cash. This plug-and-play diagnostic capability means organisations running SAP systems no longer need weeks of configuration to understand how their processes are actually performing.

Layered beneath that accessibility is the full depth of enterprise process mining that Process Intelligence has always delivered. Using SiGNAL - SAP Signavio's proprietary analytics language, analysts can perform event log extraction from both SAP and non-SAP systems, process discovery, conformance checking, real-time monitoring, and now data-driven business process simulation, enabling organisations to test the impact of process changes on their own historical data before committing to implementation. With 184 industry benchmarks and deep native integration with SAP S/4HANA and the broader SAP ecosystem, SAP Signavio Process Intelligence stands as one of the most comprehensive process mining platforms in the market.

Figure 4: Unified Process Intelligence and Mining – showing an evaluation. Alt Text: Screenshot showing the Variant Explorer for a process from Create PO Item to Record Invoice Receipt, above a table showing cycle times. The new navigation menu is shown on the left side.

Figure 5: Unified Process Intelligence and Mining – showing standardized dashboards in Process Analysis. Alt Text: Screenshot showing 7 cards of the Default Dashboard, displaying lists or tables. The top row of 3 cards contains links to various favorites (Process Flow, Performance Indicators, Correction Recommendations). The other 2x2 cards show top 5 lists: performance indicators, process flows, innovation recommendations, correction recommendations.

Find out more, and watch it in action:

  • You Asked for Simpler. SAP Signavio Listened. Here Is What Changes.
  • Video: New Harmonized Navigation Suite (12:43 min.)

 

4. Company Memory & Atoms [Beta]

As organizations scale the use of AI agents, a new opportunity emerges: making business knowledge available consistently across teams, systems, and agents. However, the procedural knowledge that governs how work should be performed is often distributed across documents, processes, policies, and other enterprise sources, making it difficult to maintain and apply at scale.

Company Memory is a centralized business knowledge layer for capturing, governing, and operationalizing this knowledge. By transforming business behaviours, controls, and policies into structured, reusable "atoms," it helps ensure more consistent, compliant, and scalable execution across the organization.

Figure 6: Company Memory. Alt Text: Screenshot of an AI-powered conversation, where the user has asked “What is the essence of SAP’s global AI ethics policy?” and the left two-thirds of the screen shows the answer. The right third shows a panel with content from an article “Develop, deploy, sell, and use AI Systems in ethical, robu…” with three tabs “Content”, “Citations”, “History”. “Content” is selected, showing sections Description, Condition, Purpose, Owner, Mandatory, and Status.

The product is built around a Hybrid UX concept, seamlessly combining conventional click-based UI with AI-assisted conversational interactions. Users can create, refine, review, and query organizational knowledge through natural language while retaining the precision and control of structured interfaces, making trusted business knowledge easy to capture, maintain and scale.

Find out more:

  • Why Enterprise Agents Need SAP Signavio’s Company Memory

 

5. AI-Powered New Signavio Process Modeler [Beta]

The new SAP Signavio Process Modeler is the next evolution of our SAP Signavio Process Manager offering. Our aim is to accelerate productivity and deliver a modern experience for customers as they model new processes. With enhanced interactions and AI-powered capabilities, this product redefines the practice of modeling and managing process landscapes, with a focus on efficiency, usability, and innovation.

The New Modeler has been shaped by years of quantitative and qualitative insight from SAP Signavio Process Manager customers, alongside ongoing innovation in AI and modeling. The result is an intelligent, seamlessly connected platform that transforms how users work, combining cutting-edge design with deep customer understanding to deliver a tool that not only meets today's complex needs but continues to evolve to unlock tomorrow's possibilities.

The following two capabilities are among the highlights:

AI assisted modelling / Autocompletion: 

Auto Suggestion and Text-to-Process bring high-quality AI capabilities to the new Modeler. As users model, Auto Suggestion picks it up, proposing the next steps of the process based on proven best practices, turning a half-finished diagram into a complete model in a fraction of the time. Throughout, the user remains in the driving seat, by editing and approving the suggested process model.

Figure 7: AI-assisted modelling. Alt-Text: Screenshot of a process model with a pop-over showing AI suggestions, listing two AI-suggested next steps “Draft Email Invite” and “Review Email Content”.

Collaborative editing

We believe that large enterprise customers need a modern process modeling platform built for how their teams actually work today and that by delivering powerful collaborative editing capabilities, we will drive stronger migration intent through a genuinely modern cloud experience. New modeler offers an intuitive well governed collaborative modeling experience that is unique on its own and covers a diverse set of our customer needs.

Figure 8: Collaborative editing. Alt Text: Screenshot of a process workspace, with an indicator bar at the top showing who else is working on it, using circles containing the user’s initials as avatars.

 

SAP User Research Panel – Your Voice Matters!

Do you use SAP products in your daily work and wish you could tell someone how to make the products you use every day even better? With the SAP User Research Panel, we provide a new way for users to give feedback directly to SAP product teams about the products they daily work with. Registration is easy and unbinding. We love to hear your opinion!
