entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 9: AI, AI, but not only! UI Design and Technology for Web and Mobile
entry.content:
This ninth and last post in my series gives an overview innovations in our UI tools and technologies, making it ever easier to design, build and integrate UIs, for both web and mobile applications. The compositional design system is powering AI-native engagement layer experiences in Joule Work. AI is making it much easier to design and code: we have a large number of innovations there, with MCP server enhancements and plug-ins for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, as well as providing the AI-powered Project Accelerator from SAP Fiori tools for ABAP too. But that’s not all, we’ve also invested in usability, performance and extensibility. We’ve also been looking at mobile development, with enhancements for web apps on mobile phones, as well as support for embedding AI into apps built with the mobile development kit.

Joule can also be seen as a technology for delivering a great user experience. To find out about recent innovations there, as well as for central entry points and services, have a look at this post, which also contains links to all the other parts of the series:

  • SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 1: AI, Joule, Mobile, SAP Build Work Zone.

In case you missed them, do have a look at my previous posts covering design and technology news, since what I mention here builds partly on what came before:

  • SAP UX Q3/2025 Update – Part 7: UI Design and Technology for Web and Mobile.
  • SAP User Experience Q1/2026 Update – Part 9: UI Design and Technology for Web and Mobile – this post introduced our MCP servers for SAPUI5 and SAP Fiori elements.

First, we’ll have a look at news for creating web UIs, before looking at what’s new for mobile design and development.

I’ve compiled the news into these sections:

  • AI Design Innovations
  • AI for UI5
  • AI for SAP Fiori tools
  • Extensibility news
  • Further news for SAPUI5 and SAP Fiori elements
  • Mobile optimized for Web
  • Mobile app development news

 

AI Design Innovations

The big news for SAP Design is our work on the compositional design system which powers Joule Work and its new engagement layer experiences, which complement existing application experiences.

Beyond that, we have introduced AI skills for designers of application experiences.

Compositional Design System for Joule Work

With Joule Work we are introducing entirely new, AI-native user experiences. We call these engagement layer experiences, which complements existing application experiences.

Figure 1: The compositional design system for AI-generated UIs. Alt Text: image depicting schematically “The compositional design system” on the left with a line linking it to a UI wireframe on the right depicted “Generated user interface”.

At the heart of Joule Work are Spaces: dynamically composed workspaces generated based on the user’s intent and context. Figure 2 shows examples of what such generated UIs looks like.

Figure 2: Examples of AI-generated UIs in Joule Work Spaces. Alt Text: Two images, one showing a desktop with a Space containing information on a return order from customer BikePros, showing status data as text, numbers and chards, the other showing a subset of the same information on a mobile phone screen.

If you want to have a look at how we are designing these new experiences, and see how we are evolving the SAP Design System for AI-driven UX, look here:

  • Designing the Autonomous Enterprise.
  • The Compositional Design System.
  • AI and Design.

If you want more information about the Joule Work user experience, have a look at my blog post:

  • SAP UX Update: The New Joule Work Engagement Layer Experiences

Skills for Designing SAP Fiori Applications

We have recently introduced several AI skills for designers using Figma. The highlight is the skill for the SAP Fiori guidelines, for web and for iOS, but we also have introduced two for the Theme Designer.

SAP Fiori guidelines design skill: Use this skill when designing, building, or reviewing SAP Fiori applications, implementing SAPUI5 or UI5 Web Components, working with SAP enterprise UX patterns, or needing guidance on buttons, forms, tables, object pages, list reports, navigation, messaging, colors, typography, accessibility, AI/Joule integration, or any SAP Fiori UI element.

  • SAP Fiori guidelines design skill in SAP AI skills library

SAP Fiori for iOS design skill: Converts Figma designs from the SAP Fiori iOS UI Kit into correct SwiftUI prototype code with Fiori color tokens, typography, animations, and component guidelines. Use this skill when a designer provides a Figma node ID or component name and wants working SwiftUI code, when asking which Fiori iOS component to use, when mapping Figma variants to SwiftUI, or when adding animations and state transitions to iOS prototypes.

  • SAP Fiori for iOS design skill in SAP AI skills library

Theme Designer skills: we have introduced these two skills, one for providing guidance on usng tokens from the design system, the other providing help based on the documentation:

  • UI Theme Designer Design Tokens skill
  • UI Theme Designer Help skill

 

AI for UI5

This last half year our engineers have been focusing on AI: how can we enable you to create apps faster and better with the help of AI. The main investments have been in providing or improving our MCP servers, providing plug-ins to enable agents, and bringing AI to ABAP development too.

UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot)

In April we introduced the UI plugins for Claude. These have since been generalized, so that they are not limited to Claude Code, and renamed to “UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents”, supporting GitHub Copilot in addition to Claude Code.

Figure 3: Alt Text: Image with Claude and GitHub icons above the text “UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents” – “New Release” – “Start your UI5 journey with Copilot and Claude”.

What can you do with these plugins? Let’s have a look…

UI5 Plugin — Your UI5 Development Companion

The UI5 plugin equips coding agents with deep knowledge of the SAPUI5 and OpenUI5 ecosystem. It helps you with the following tasks:

  • Create new UI5 projects: Create scaffolded project structures based on best practices without any manual setup.
  • Detect and fix UI5-specific errors: Claude understands UI5 linting rules and applies fixes based on the official guidelines.
  • Access UI5 API documentation: Get accurate, framework-aware answers about controls, modules, events, and APIs instead of generic JavaScript suggestions.

The UI5 plugin was recently enhanced with these three new skills, and also made available for GitHub Copilot:

  • UI Integration Cards: UI Integration Cards have very specific rules around data placement, binding syntax, and manifest structure. This new skill encodes those rules so the agent can get cards right without trial and error.
  • OPA5 integration tests: Writing reliable OPA5 tests requires knowing the actual control tree of the running app — something a coding agent can't derive from source alone. This skill bridges that gap. It also covers initial test configuration, multi-view setups, page object organization, and teardown patterns.
  • UI5 Tables: This skill helps agents get tables right, by enforcing essential patterns and production-ready handling for performance, personalization, drag and drop, and data type alignment.

UI5 TypeScript Conversion plugin — Migrate to TypeScript with Confidence
Migrating a JavaScript UI5 project to TypeScript can be tricky. Generic AI tools often handle the required transformations incorrectly. The UI5 TypeScript Conversion plugin provides coding agents with a step-by-step conversion playbook.

UI5 Modernization Plugin: ​Keeping your SAPUI5 or OpenUI5 app up to date just got easier. The new UI5 Modernization Plugin automates the most time-consuming parts of app modernization: replacing deprecated APIs, eliminating global namespaces, updating manifest.json and Component.js, and getting your app ready for Content Security Policy compliance. The plugin is available as a Claude Code plugin and in the GitHub Copilot marketplace.

Find out more here:

  • Introducing UI5 Plugins for Claude: AI-Powered Development for SAPUI5 and OpenUI5
  • UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents: Now Supporting GitHub Copilot (with details on the three recently added skills decribed above)
  • Introducing the UI5 Modernization Plugin: Modernize Your OpenUI5/SAPUI5 App in Hours, Not Weeks

UI5 MCP Server News

If you don’t want to use the above UI5 Modernization Plugin, you can use the UI5 MCP server with GitHub Copilot. Find out more here:

The agent does most of the work, and you can focus on code review.https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/how-to-migrate-ui5-projects-to-the-latest-ui5-best-practices/ba-p/14340388

This blog post focuses on how the UI5 MCP server can support you in migrating your UI5 project easily to the latest best practices with the help of GitHub Copilot Coding Agent. Migrate your project.

ABAP AI in SAP Joule for Developers

Although this is not directly UI related, a good user experience of course relies on good back-end services, which are often built with ABAP. Hence I’d like to mention that ABAP AI capabilities including agentic capabilities is now offered as a service across SAP BTP ABAP Environment, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition for releases 2021 and higher. Find out more here:

  • SAP Joule for Developers, ABAP AI capabilities including agentic capabilities is now available!

 

AI for SAP Fiori Tools

Project Accelerator for ABAP Cloud

The Project Accelerator supports rapid prototyping with AI, based on images and/or a requirements description. It has been available for CAP (SAP Cloud Application Programming Model) since 2024, where it can generate database tables, OData services and UIs from a sketch or a description.

Now, you have the same power for ABAP development following the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) – for SAP Business AI Platform as well as for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Figure 4: SAP Fiori tools project accelerator. Alt Text: three images on the left: a high-fidelity Figma model, a lower fidelity screenshot, and a sketch on paper, with an pointy bracket leading to the text “Use SAP Fiori tools project accelerator to generate the app”. On the right an extract of the accelerator’s screen, showing a thumbnail of an uploaded image.

Find out more here:

  • Develop RAP-Based SAP Fiori Applications in Minutes with SAP Fiori Tools AI Project Accelerator

MCP Server and Skills for SAP Fiori

MCP News for SAP Fiori

AI-Chat in SAP Business Application Studio for SAP Fiori: SAP Business Application Studio now includes an AI Chat capability that you can use for MCP-supported AI-driven SAP Fiori development directly from the browser. 

Installing the MCP server locally: For local development, the MCP server for SAP Fiori is now available through the MCP registry on GitHub. You can also install it as a Claude plugin, together with our new skills (more on that below).

Full Stack AI-Driven Development in VS Code:  The MCP server for SAP Fiori pairs with the new ABAP MCP server, which is part of the ABAP development tools for Visual Studio Code. Together, the two bridge the gap between backend ABAP services and the SAP Fiori frontend, enabling a true fullstack AI-driven development experience from within VS Code. For more details, watch Christoph Gollmick’s ABAPConf presentation:

  • AI-Powered Full-Stack Dev with SAP’s MCP Servers for ABAP & SAP Fiori

Skills for SAP Fiori

We have now published the first set of skills that complement the MCP server for SAP Fiori:

  • SAP Fiori app development: Guides the creation and modification of SAP Fiori elements applications in CAP and standalone projects
  • Analytical chart: Adds an analytical chart and table hybrid to a List Report, supporting CAP and ABAP RAP (OData V4)
  • Visual filter: Adds chart-based visual filters to the filter bar or value help in SAP Fiori elements applications
  • Create CLI: Runs and automates the CLI for generating, converting, and managing Fiori projects
  • ESLint plug-in: Configures, migrates, or runs ESLint with the ESLint plugin for SAP Fiori tools in SAP Fiori projects.

 

Extensibility for Key Users and Developers

Key User Adaptation and Transition to Developer Extensibility

Apparently, many customers are still not aware of all the great options we provide for users to adapt the UI without needing to ask IT administrators for support.

A key user is a business expert who is authorized to make changes on behalf of other users — for example a team member who is interested in technology. The goal of key user extensibility is to empower business users to be able to adapt their working environment to suit their needs, without having to rely on system administrators.

This nice overview blog post explains how to use it, and also explains how you can easily transition from key user extensibility to developer extensibility:

  • Key User Adaptation: Powerful New Features & Seamless Transition to Developer Extensibility.

Have a look at this video to see it in action:

  • Video: Extending SAP Fiori Object Pages with Adapt UI (13:26 min.)

Adapting UIs for Specific User Roles now available on SAP Business AI Platform

Great news for BTP developers! The SAPUI5 Flexibility features described in this blog post are now available on the SAP BTP Cloud Foundry environment starting with UI5 version 1.146:

  • SAPUI5 Flexibility: Adapting UIs for Specific User Roles.

New Name: UI5 Flexibility Service

We have renamed „UI5 flexibility for key users“ to „UI flexibility service”.

We did this because we had introduced end user personalization capabilities in addition to key user adaptation, so the name became rather misleading. Find out more in this blog post:

  • More Power, New Name: The UI Flexibility Service Explained

 

Further News for UI5 and SAP Fiori elements

Developing apps with modern concepts: guidance for developers

Developers often need to balance development efficiency, maintenance costs, and design flexibility when building enterprise-ready applications with SAP Fiori elements and freestyle SAPUI5. With the introduction of Building Blocks a while ago we offer a lot of flexibility, so that you can choose the approach that fits your needs best. To help you make the right decision, we have created this guidance for you:

  • Developing Apps with Modern Concepts: Guidance for Developers

The SAP Fiori development portal that I introduced in my previous post is your entry point for discovering the various options in detail and starting your development. This is described in this series of blog posts in more detail:

  • Introducing the SAP Fiori Development Portal: Your Gateway to Rapid SAP Fiori App Creation (1 of 6).

TypeScript 6 and 7 – What UI5 TypeScript developers need to know in 2026

TypeScript is going through its biggest transition in years - and if you build UI5 applications with TypeScript, here we have all the details you need to know.

Read about it in this blog post.

Usability Improvements in SAP Fiori Tools

The 2603 release brought several usability improvements:

  • Direct navigation to source in the manifest gives developers a more transparent editing experience.
  • New walkthrough for getting started makes novice developers more productive more quickly (see Figure 5).
  • Import key user changes into an Adaptation Project and keep your edits (as already described above in the section on Extensibility).

Figure 5: Walkthrough for SAP Fiori tools. Alt Text: Image of the welcome screen, with a list of topics on the left, with “What is SAP Fiori Tools?” selected. On the right a description text with five bullet points.

Learn more about these improvements here:

  • SAP Fiori Tools 2603 Update: RAP Project Accelerator, Walkthrough, Adaptation Improvements, and More

Renovations and Performance Improvements in SAP Fiori Tools

The latest release of SAP Fiori tools brings quite a few renovations and performance improvements. Highlights are:

  • Moving from CommonJS to ECMAScript Modules
  • ESLint 10 upgrade
  • 80% faster extension startup.

Have a look at these in more detail, along with another six smaller improvements:

  • SAP Fiori Tools 2607 Update: Skills, Fullstack AI Development, and Performance

 

Mobile optimized for Web

The SAP Fiori elements team has been working on optimizing the user experience of web-based SAP Fiori elements apps for mobile phone users. If you use SAP Joule mobile app (formerly SAP Mobile Start), it gives you a list of all SAP applications available to you – both native mobile apps as well as web apps, such as those from SAP S/4HANA Cloud. Tapping on one of these web apps will launch the app directly, so as a user you don’t notice that it is running in a browser.

This is currently available to customers via this Early Adopter Care (EAC) program. If you are interested, do sign up, registration ends November 28, 2026.

As you can see in Figure 6, the layout for lists and object pages is more intuitive than before.

Figure 6: SAP Fiori elements mobile phone optimization (EAC), with a list report on the left, an object page on the right. Alt Text: two mobile phone images for the app Manage Product Costing, the list showing three entries each with product ID, name, category, supplier and price shown. The object page shows the header and two tabs, with General Information selected, showing the Order Details section and part of the Admin Data section.

Re-imagining filters on mobile using natural language

Filter bars are great on a desktop, but using them on a mobile phone is a real challenge. Now that we have natural language AI-assisted Easy Filters, perhaps we can use natural language to get a much better filtering experience on mobile phones? This is precisely what our engineering teams are looking into (Figure 6).

Figure 7: Traditional filter bar on a mobile phone compared to AI-powered natural language filter. Alt Text: two mobile phone screens, on the left a list of filter names to select, on the right an Easy Filter text entry field above buttons “Recent” and “Favorites”.

Find out more here, and sign up for the Early Adopter Care program if you want to try it out and give us feedback:

  • Reimagining Filters on Mobile: A Natural Language Approach in SAP Fiori Elements

 

Mobile App Development News

SAP Fiori for Android and SAP Fiori for iOS 26.4 Release Updates

The SAP BTP SDK for iOS and the SAP BTP SDK for Android have shipped their 26.4 releases, each containing several feature enhancements to these components:

  • List Picker Form Cell (iOS and Android)
  • Switch Form Cell (iOS and Android)
  • Step Progress Indicator (Android only)
  • Hyperlinked Text Style (Android only)

Find out more here:

  • What’s New for SAP BTP SDK for iOS 26.4
  • What’s New for SAP BTP SDK for Android 26.4

Mobile development kit (MDK)

The last two releases have brought some nice new features, with two important ones for enabling embedded AI in mobile apps. In the following sections I’d like to highlight these:

  • Contact Cell control enhancements
  • AI Notice Form Cell Control
  • AI Feedback Form Cell Control
  • Stepper Form Cell Control
  • Enhanced Offline OData Progress Feedback

Contact Cell control enhancements

The ContactCell component now supports:

  • User Initials: displaying user initials, which is used when profile pictures are not available.
  • BadgeImage: this new property allows you to attach an additional indicator icon or image to the existing DetailImage or DetailImageText for each contact. For example, it can be used to highlight and identify primary contacts in a contact list.

Figure 8: Contact Cell control enhancements. Alt Text: iPhone and Android phone screens showing list of contacts with indicator icon with initials for each.

Find out more here:

  • Contact Cell control enhancements

AI Notice Form Cell Control

As part of ongoing enhancements in embedded AI capabilities, a new FormCell control, AINoticeFormCell, is introduced to display an inline notice for AI-generated content that may require review before use. 

Key Benefits:

  • Clearly indicates when content is generated using AI.
  • Helps users understand that AI-generated content may need validation.
  • Supports optional links for additional context or guidance.

Figure 9: AI notice form cell control. Alt Text: iPhone and Android phone screens showing various short and long AI notice messages such as “This result was produced by an AI model. Verify before use.”

Find out more here:

  • AI Notice Form Cell Control

AI Feedback Form Cell Control

As part of the embedded AI enhancement area, a new FormCell control, AIFeedback, is introduced to enable quick user feedback on AI-generated content. The control provides thumbs-up and thumbs-down options along with a caption and is designed specifically for AI-related experiences.

Figure 10: AI feedback form cell control. Alt Text: iPhone and Android phone screens showing various options for thumbs up and down feedback selectors.

Find out more here:

  • AI Feedback Form Cell Control

Stepper Form Cell Control

We have introduced a new FormCell control, Stepper, to allow users to increase or decrease numeric values using buttons or direct input. The control supports configurable step size, value range limits, decimal precision, and validation.

Key Benefits:

  • Enables easy adjustment of numeric values through stepper buttons or manual entry.
  • Supports configurable increments for flexible use cases.
  • Allows enforcement of minimum and maximum value limits.
  • Provides control over numeric precision for consistent input formatting.

Figure 11: Stepper Form Control. iPhone and Android phone screens showing three different stepper controls with + and – selectors and the value in between, with a popover showing “Alert: Stepper value is 4” and an OK button.

Find out more here:

  • Stepper Form Cell Control

Enhanced Offline OData Progress Indicator For Long-Running Tasks

Offline OData operations now provide step-level progress messages, offering improved visibility into long-running tasks such as initialization, download, upload, and send store. Localized default messages are displayed automatically with no additional configuration.

Key Benefits:

  • Introduces step-level progress updates for offline operations.
  • Improves visibility into long-running processes such as sync and data transfer.
  • Provides localized default messages out of the box.
  • Enables customization and runtime control of progress feedback.
  • Progress messages can be customized using the ProgressMessages property under OfflineOptions in the .service definition. These messages are used during offline operations including initialization, download, upload, and send store.

Figure 12: Offline progress indicator. Animated video of iPad and Android phone screens showing progress over time of a 20 step process, with the current step counter being incremented along with a text for each step.

Find out more here:

  • Enhanced Offline OData Progress Feedback.

Further MDK updates

I picked the above highlights, but there are quite a few more enhancements in the last two MDK releases. To get the full overview, have a look at these two blog posts:

  • What’s new in Mobile development kit client 26.3
  • What’s new in Mobile development kit client 26.6

 

Further Information

This year’s UI5con 2026 on July 14th was a great success. If you want to hear the experts talking about UI5, UI5 Flexibility, SAP Fiori elements, and SAP Fiori tools in much more detail, then watch the recordings of the sessions:

entry.title: Screen Personas in CE2608: Smarter Flavor Management and Option to Define Custom Industrial Devices
entry.content:
Screen Personas in CE2608 introduces enhancements that make it easier to reuse existing flavors and deliver optimized user experiences across specialized devices. 

Two capabilities stand out: 

  1. Copy a Flavor to Multiple Target Flavors 
  2. Option to Define Custom Industrial Device Types 

Together, these enhancements help organizations reduce flavor development effort, improve consistency, and better support specialized hardware used in industrial environments. 

  1. Copy a Flavor to Multiple Target Flavors 

Managing multiple flavors that share a common layout can often involve repetitive work. This is now simplified by enhancing the existing “Copy to Application ID” functionality and renaming it to “Copy to Application ID or Flavor ID.” 

With this enhancement, administrators can copy a source flavor to an existing target flavor. More importantly, the same source flavor can be copied to multiple target flavors in a single operation, provided that the screen ID and Program Name matches the target flavors. 

Why Is This Useful? 

Consider a business scenario where you already have a Manage flavor and need similar Display and Create flavors. 

Instead of building the Display and Create flavors from scratch, you can: 

  • Start with the existing Manage flavor as the source. 
  • Copy it to the target flavors. 
  • Make only the required modifications. 

This approach promotes consistency across flavors while significantly reducing development and maintenance effort. 

Prerequisites 

The following conditions apply: 

  • The user must have the Personas Administrator role. 
  • Target flavors must already exist. They can be empty or contain existing changes. 
  • The source flavor must not contain an adaptive stack. 
  • The screen ID and Program Name of the source flavor must match the target flavors. 

Additional Option for BDT Application Flavors 

CE2608 also introduces an option specifically useful for BDT (Business Data Toolset) application flavors. 

BDT transactions can have similar detail screens while using different entry screens. In such scenarios, administrators can choose to skip entry-screen changes during the copy operation. 

This makes it possible to reuse the relevant flavor changes while preserving the target transaction's existing initial-screen behavior. 

Key Benefit 

This enhancement transforms flavor copying from a one-to-one activity into a more efficient mass flavor reuse mechanism, making it particularly valuable in environments with many similar flavors. It also enables users to work on a new flavor and subsequently overwrite or replace an existing flavor without impacting its existing sharing configurations, eliminating the need to reconfigure sharing settings. 

 

  1. Option to Define Custom Industrial Device Types 

SAP Screen Personas already supports adaptive flavors that are created based on the dimensions and characteristics of the target device. 

With CE2608, this capability becomes significantly more flexible. 

Previously, the available device list was static and maintained by SAP. With CE2608, administrators can now define and register their own custom devices for adaptive flavor creation. 

Why Do Custom Devices Matter? 

Industrial organizations often use specialized hardware that does not correspond to standard consumer devices. 

Examples include: 

  • Rugged handheld terminals 
  • Industrial tablets 
  • Warehouse scanners 
  • Shop-floor devices 
  • Specialized company-specific hardware 

These devices can have unique screen dimensions and pixel densities. A flavor optimized for a standard desktop or tablet may not provide the best experience on such hardware. 

CE2608 addresses this by allowing administrators to define custom devices and specify attributes such as: 

  • Device width 
  • Device height 
  • Pixel ratio 

These parameters are then used to define an adaptive flavor for the custom device. 

Creating Adaptive Flavors for Custom Devices 

Once a custom device has been registered by the administrator, it becomes available in the device selection list when creating an adaptive flavor. 

This allows flavor designers to explicitly design and optimize the user experience for the organization's actual hardware landscape. 

Key Benefits 

Better Support for Industrial Scenarios 

Organizations can optimize SAP GUI experiences for rugged devices, scanners, industrial tablets, and other specialized hardware. 

Improved Responsive Behavior 

Device-specific width, height, and pixel-ratio information allows adaptive flavors to be rendered appropriately for the target hardware. 

Greater Flexibility 

Organizations are no longer limited to the predefined device list when designing adaptive flavors. 

Conclusion 

Screen Personas in CE2608 makes flavor management more scalable and adaptive. 

The ability to copy one flavor to multiple target flavors reduces repetitive configuration and encourages reuse. At the same time, custom industrial device support extends adaptive flavors beyond SAP's predefined device list, allowing organizations to optimize classic SAP applications for their specific hardware environments. 

For organizations managing large flavor landscapes or supporting specialized industrial devices, these enhancements can translate into less development effort, greater consistency, and a better user experience. 

 

Learn more about SAP Screen Personas
  • Online training. The best way to learn the basics about SAP Screen Personas (Adapt UI for classic applications) is to take our free training course on the learning.sap.com platform: https://learning.sap.com/courses/adapting-the-ui-in-sap-s-4hana-cloud-using-sap-screen-personas
  • Connect with your peers. Every other month, we have a group of customers that gather online to share best practices, demo their flavors, and answer each other’s questions. Experts from the product team also join to explain how to use the latest functionality. If you are interested in joining, you can sign up online to join the SAP Screen Personas practitioner forum. This will add you to the mailing list for the monthly meeting summaries. Please contact “Peter Spielvogel“ or me directly if you want to join the monthly calls.
  • Product documentation. The SAP Screen Personas documentation, provides more clear , comprehensive and the latest information about the product.

entry.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Searching or Viewing Support Cases in SAP for Me
entry.content:
Are you having trouble viewing or managing your support cases in SAP for Me? This SAP Blog post is for you! 

 

 

 

Managing support cases shouldn’t feel like a maze. If you’re an SAP customer or partner, SAP for Me is your central hub — a one-stop portal where you can track, manage, and customize your support cases with ease. 

 

Here's a step-by-step guide on how to view or search for your support cases in SAP for Me.  

  1.  Login to SAP for Me using your S-user ID and password.  
  2. Under “Dashboards”, click on “Services & Support”.  
  3. Click on the “Cases” tab, to view your case list.

 

 

 

 

 

 

With the newly designed Case List, you will see two views: Default view and Personal view. 

Under Default view, you will see several case selection options: 

  • Open Cases - created by someone in your organization and that, based on your authorizations, you have access to view 
  • Closed Cases - were resolved and confirmed 
  • Drafts - have not been sent to SAP yet 
  • Favorites - case(s) marked as Favorite 
  • Auto Confirm - case(s) that will auto confirm soon 

You can sort and group the list, choose which type of cases shall be displayed, and narrow down the items to those most relevant to you by using a variety of filter criteria. This configuration can then be saved for future re-use, allowing you to switch between different views with ease.   

 

You may refer to this article Customizing the Case List help topic or refer to the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 2931236 for guidance on managing and customizing your case list. 

 

Additionally, using the central search box, you can filter or search for the specific case number as per the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3363874 - How to search for a specific case number - SAP for Me. 

 

For more information, please refer to the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 1812813- How to view or search for cases - SAP for Me. 

 

________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Authorization Requirements: 

 Ensure your S-user ID must have the appropriate authorizations to manage and view support cases in SAP for Me. See Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3383142 - Which S-user ID authorizations are required for support case handling? 

To request the necessary authorizations, use the self-service process described in the Knowledge Base article (KBA) 2891528 or, contact your super administrator directly. See the super administrators in the company here: Users & Contacts - SAP for Me . 

________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Good News!  Meet Joule: Your AI Assistant

 

Did you know you can now search and view your support cases effortlessly using our newly integrated AI-powered driven “Joule” in SAP for Me?  

Yes, you read that right! SAP for Me now features Joule, an AI-powered assistant that transforms how you manage your cases. Instead of hunting for specific pages, you can simply type your intent, and Joule will direct you to the right dashboard in SAP for Me.  

 

Here’s how it works:  

1. Click the diamond icon (Joule) in the upper right corner of your screen, next to the notification bell, or use the banner to start typing your query.

 

 

2. Joule will analyze your request and display the specific case record. 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Note:  In addition to the cases you reported, Joule can also search and display support cases submitted by your colleagues or your SAP Partner under your company’s account.  

3. Click the case number to manage and open the case details. 

 

For more information and to better understand Joule in SAP for Me — its features, scope, and capabilities — you may refer to Knowledge Base article (KBA) 3740053 - Joule in SAP for Me - Scope and FAQ.  

 

You can also visit the SAP News Center https://news.sap.com/2026/06/sap-launches-joule-in-sap-for-me/ to learn more and subscribe to the newsletter for updates.  

 

And that’s it! Viewing and searching for cases in SAP for Me is straightforward once you know where to look. Whether you’re tracking an ongoing issue or reviewing a resolved case for reference, the Cases feature in SAP for Me puts all the information you need right at your fingertips. 

 

 

Got More Questions? 

 Please note that the Customer Interaction Center is always happy to guide you on any of the mentioned processes and assist you with any queries you may have!    
 

If you have any questions, please feel free to ask us in the Q&A  All Questions in Customer Experience | SAP Community and All Questions in Support Services | SAP Community  

 

Don't Miss Out on Free Webcasts  

 

 

 

 

We would like to invite you to our free webcasts, which we believe can help you get the best from your support in SAP. You can find all upcoming CIC Webcasts. These sessions are open to all the users and will revolve around hot topics in support today such as SAP for Me, Case Management, etc.  

Additionally, you can explore a range of CIC how-to videos at learning.sap.com. Please feel free to share this information with your colleagues. We are looking forward to your attendance.  

 

Lastly, you may want to access all CIC Blogs here:  https://community.sap.com/t5/tag/CustomerInteractionCenter/tg-p/board-id/crm-blog-sap.  

Thanks for reading!  We hope you found this guide helpful.

entry.title: Joule Work on the Go and Mobile Design System Enhancements: What's New in SAP's Mobile Experience
entry.content:
In the first half of this year, SAP Fiori for Android and SAP Fiori for iOS as well as Joule mobile client have undergone a series of intelligent improvements aimed at elevating user experience and boosting productivity. These enhancements have introduced greater flexibility, consistency, and functionality across both platforms, ensuring that users can navigate their applications with ease and efficiency.

On top of that, the Joule Work app, formerly known as SAP Mobile Start, has been introduced at SAP Sapphire. With this app, complex tasks can be accomplished while on the go. Users simply need to define their goals and let AI take action.

 

Joule Work Mobile App

Joule Work is a central, intelligent workspace where AI takes charge of the busy work, enabling users to focus on driving outcomes. It transforms the work environment with a proactive, outcome-driven experience, where users articulate goals and AI coordinates actions across systems to accomplish them efficiently. Processes speed up considerably with proactive assistance, using the comprehensive business context of Joule Agents and Joule Assistants to highlight relevant data and suggest actions. This setup streamlines complexity, allowing users to focus on decision-making and outcome generation, while routine tasks are delegated to supervised agents. In addition to the web app, Joule Work offers a desktop app for faster access to local files and applications, as well as a mobile app for managing complex workflows on the go.

Conversations

Conversations act as dynamic interfaces for seamless interaction with Joule, making engagement intuitive and natural. Users can easily express their needs by typing, speaking, or attaching files, eliminating the need for traditional navigation methods. Joule enriches this process by offering context-based prompts, conducting platform-wide searches, and providing detailed answers with real-time data and interactive elements. By facilitating dialogue, conversations enable users to express their intentions and explore desired outcomes, drawing together insights and results from SAP and third-party systems. Moreover, conversations serve as entry points to spaces, supporting more complex workflows. This streamlined approach enhances user engagement and simplifies the pursuit of information and task completion.

Spaces

Spaces are dynamic, AI-generated workspaces tailored to match a user's intent, offering a seamless user experience. These adaptable environments allow users to engage in conversations and customize features without navigating through apps or dashboards, ensuring that individual needs are met efficiently. Within a space, tasks can be completed using natural language or structured inputs, fostering intuitive and effective interactions. Spaces are created in real time, pulling together the necessary data, tools, and context to achieve specific goals. They display only essential information through actionable summary cards, tables, metrics, or alerts, enabling users to focus on their tasks without distractions. These persistent spaces ensure users can easily return to continue their work from where they left off, facilitating both simple and complex problem-solving with ease.

Download for Android | Download for iOS

 

Joule mobile client 

The Joule mobile client, which facilitates the integration of Joule into Joule Work, provides exciting new features designed to enhance user interaction and streamline communication. Dictation allows users to harness the power of their device's built-in voice recognition, enabling hands-free messaging and smoother, more accessible conversation workflows with Joule. This innovation is perfect for busy professionals who need to multitask, as it allows them to communicate effortlessly without sacrificing productivity. The newly integrated typeahead feature intelligently offers contextual suggestions as users type. This predictive element cuts down on keystrokes and expedites prompt completion, resulting in more efficient interactions. Alongside these input features, Joule has also expanded its functionality with response actions, enabling users to easily copy or regenerate responses directly within the conversation. This means users can quickly reuse Joule's outputs or request new answers without retyping prompts, offering a seamless, user-friendly experience. Additionally, the transparency and explainability feature has been improved to provide users with clearer insights into Joule's AI-generated replies, ensuring they understand the response origins and details. Sources are now displayed separately from response insights, giving users straightforward access to the information that influences their conversations. Together, these updates demonstrate Joule’s commitment to enhancing user productivity and communication efficiency through innovative solutions while ensuring clarity and confidence in AI interactions.

 

What’s New in SAP Fiori for Android 26.1 and 26.4

Extended Card Header

The extended card header has been updated for greater flexibility, enabling you to place various components, such as tags, status indicators, or custom elements, together in a single row. This allows for more compact, streamlined, and versatile card layouts.

For more information, check out Card Header in the SAP Fiori for Android design guidelines.

Extended card header

Multi-User Onboarding

The user list now reflects SAP Fiori for iOS standards and displays users onboarded to a specific device, sorted from the earliest to the most recent.

For more information, check out Multi-User Onboarding.

Switching or adding a user

Step Progress Indicator

The nodes in the step progress indicator, which is designed to track and display a user's status within a user flow, now offer the same customization options as SAP BTP SDK for iOS. You can modify the size, layout, and icon in an icon node and specify different states for the icon node. When there are just a few steps, the width of each step expands to fill the screen, creating a more balanced layout.

Refer to Step Progress Indicator to find out more about this component.

Step progress indicator

List Picker Form Cell

A read-only state has been added to the list picker form cell, which allows for the selection of one or more options among values within a defined category. In this state, the selected value(s) are shown, and the chevron is removed. The cell height adjusts to ensure that all selected values are displayed without any truncation.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cell

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell, which allows users to turn on/off individual settings, now includes a read-only state. In this state, the toggle switch control is replaced with a text label that indicates the pre-set value. While the default label is “On/Off,” you can customize it to provide more contextual messages, such as "Included/Not Included."

See Switches for more details.

Switch form cell

 

What’s New in iOS 26.1 and 26.4

AI User Feedback

The AI user feedback feature lets users share their experiences with AI. The inline AI feedback entry point has been updated to function as a standalone, reusable component.

See AI User Feedback for more information.

AI inline user feedback

Step Progress Indicator

The step progress indicator, which monitors and shows a user's position within a user flow, has been enhanced. The width of each step node is now adaptable with a set minimum value, allowing the indicator to expand and fill the screen width when there are fewer steps visible.

Explore the Step Progress Indicator.

Step progress indicator nodes

List Picker Form Cell

The list picker now features a read-only state where selected values appear inline, the chevron is removed, and the cell becomes non-interactive. There is no word limit on displayed values. However, lengthy or multi-selected values might cause the cell height to stretch. To address this, we recommend either avoiding the read-only state or implementing a custom summary view.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cells

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell now includes a read-only state where a text label, defaulting to "On/Off," is shown instead of the visual switch. This label is fully customizable to offer more contextual messaging, such as "Included/Not Included." The form cell height and padding are consistent with the active state, ensuring a seamless layout experience.

Read more about the Switch Form Cell.

Switch form cell

 

UI Kits for Figma

SAP Fiori for Android and iOS UI Kit

With the updated SAP Fiori for Android and iOS UI Kits, it’s now easier than ever to use the latest components and patterns in your mobile design. By using the UI Kits, you can quickly create a consistent user experience that enables app implementations at scale.

SAP Fiori for Android UI Kits | SAP Fiori for iOS UI Kits

entry.title: Enhancing SAP Fiori Elements with Contact Quick Views Using OData V4 Annotations
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

Introduction

The SAP Fiori Elements List Report is a standard, highly efficient floorplan for displaying tabular data with built-in filtering, sorting, and object page navigation. However, a common business requirement is to provide users with immediate contextual details—like organization names and full addresses—without forcing them to navigate away to a separate object page. Out of the box, standard text columns don't offer this inline detail.

This guide covers a complete, working implementation to configure a Contact Quick View popover directly from a List Report table using:

  • OData V4 XML annotations (@Communication.Contact) for the blueprint

  • UI.DataFieldForAnnotation for rendering the smart link

  • Zero custom UI5 JavaScript or XML fragments

  • Northwind OData service

 

Why I Wrote This

Recently, I wanted to improve the frontend user experience of a standard Fiori Elements List Report by reducing unnecessary navigation and clicks. The moment I started researching the best way to implement a Quick View popover from a table column, I realized many guides pointed toward heavy frontend customizations.

Most documentation either suggested writing custom XML fragments with sap.m.Popover, binding standard UI5 sap.m.Link controls with complex press events, or extending the controller. This post walks through the complete, robust, code-free flow: using pure metadata to define the contact structure and instructing the framework to render it as a smart, interactive popover.

 

Prerequisites

  • Basic understanding of SAP Fiori Elements and OData V4 metadata.

  • An OData service exposing customer data (such as the Northwind service).

 

Step 1: Importing the Required Vocabularies

To use UI and Communication annotations in our OData V4 EDMX file, we must first reference the standard SAP vocabularies. Ensure our <edmx:Edmx> document includes references to Common, UI, and Communication:

<edmx:Reference Uri="https://sap.github.io/odata-vocabularies/vocabularies/Common.xml">
    <edmx:Include Namespace="com.sap.vocabularies.Common.v1" Alias="Common"/>
</edmx:Reference>
<edmx:Reference Uri="https://sap.github.io/odata-vocabularies/vocabularies/UI.xml">
    <edmx:Include Namespace="com.sap.vocabularies.UI.v1" Alias="UI"/>
</edmx:Reference>
<edmx:Reference Uri="https://sap.github.io/odata-vocabularies/vocabularies/Communication.xml">
    <edmx:Include Namespace="com.sap.vocabularies.Communication.v1" Alias="Communication"/>
</edmx:Reference>

 

Step 2: Defining the @Communication.Contact Annotation

The @Communication.Contact term acts as the blueprint for the Quick View popover. I apply this annotation directly to the target entity, NorthwindModel.Customer.

Notice how I map the formatted name (fn) to the CustomerID. Because the fn property acts as the primary identifier in the UI, mapping it to CustomerID ensures that the ID string itself becomes the clickable link in our table. I then map the organization (org) and the work address (adr).

<Annotations Target="NorthwindModel.Customer">
    <Annotation Term="Communication.Contact">
        <Record>
            <!-- Map fn to CustomerID so the ID string becomes the clickable link -->
            <PropertyValue Property="fn" Path="CustomerID"/>
            
            <PropertyValue Property="org" Path="CompanyName"/>
            <PropertyValue Property="adr">
                <Collection>
                    <Record>
                        <PropertyValue Property="type" EnumMember="Communication.ContactInformationType/work"/>
                        <PropertyValue Property="street" Path="Address"/>
                        <PropertyValue Property="locality" Path="City"/>
                        <PropertyValue Property="country" Path="Country"/>
                        <PropertyValue Property="code" Path="PostalCode"/>
                    </Record>
                </Collection>
            </PropertyValue>
        </Record>
    </Annotation>

 

Step 3: Integrating the Quick View into the Table

Now that the contact structure is defined, we need to instruct the Fiori Elements application to render it inside the List Report table. I configure this within the @UI.LineItem collection.

Instead of using a standard UI.DataField for the Customer ID, I use a UI.DataFieldForAnnotation. By pointing the Target property to the @Communication.Contact annotation I just created, the framework handles the rest. The remaining columns are added as standard data fields.

<!-- Table Layout -->
    <Annotation Term="UI.LineItem">
        <Collection>
            <!-- DataFieldForAnnotation triggers the smart link and pop-up functionality -->
            <Record Type="UI.DataFieldForAnnotation">
                <PropertyValue Property="Target" AnnotationPath="@Communication.Contact"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="Customer ID"/>
            </Record>
            
            <Record Type="UI.DataField">
                <PropertyValue Property="Value" Path="CompanyName"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="Company Name"/>
            </Record>

            <Record Type="UI.DataField">
                <PropertyValue Property="Value" Path="Address"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="Address"/>
            </Record>

            <Record Type="UI.DataField">
                <PropertyValue Property="Value" Path="City"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="City"/>
            </Record>

            <Record Type="UI.DataField">
                <PropertyValue Property="Value" Path="Country"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="Country"/>
            </Record>

            <Record Type="UI.DataField">
                <PropertyValue Property="Value" Path="PostalCode"/>
                <PropertyValue Property="Label" String="Postal Code"/>
            </Record>
        </Collection>
    </Annotation>
</Annotations>

 

Output:

 

A Few Things to Keep in Mind:

  • Metadata Caching: Browsers heavily cache metadata. When developing locally, ensure to disable the cache via our network tab so UI updates render correctly.

  • Vocabulary Validation: Strictly adhere to OData V4 namespaces (Communication.v1, UI.v1). Mixing V2 and V4 schemas will break the smart link binding.

 

Conclusion

Deploying these annotations instantly transforms the static "Customer ID" column into interactive Fiori smart links. Clicking these links triggers a standard QuickView popover containing the mapped @Communication.Contact properties, including the Customer ID, Department, and Address. By leveraging UI.DataFieldForAnnotation and pure OData V4 metadata, we completely bypass custom controller extensions and XML fragment parsing. This metadata-driven architecture ensures our UI remains lightweight, easily maintainable, and perfectly aligned with Fiori design guidelines.

entry.title: Designing AI around Human Cognition
entry.content:
For nearly two decades, we designed software that people learned to operate. We built dashboards, tables, filters, settings, menus, and navigation. To get to an answer, people learned where information lived, which control to use, which page to open, and which application to switch to next. Over time, we became very good at it. We did not just learn the interface. We learned how to think in the structure of the software.

Then AI arrived. Suddenly, the system could produce more intelligence, more analysis, and more possibilities gave in seconds. And there is a very natural temptation: take all of that intelligence and put it back into the interface we already know. Another list. Another cards. Another recommendation. Another button. AI on the surface. SaaS underneath.

We are designing below interface. We are designing the collaboration. AI can keep producing. People still have to make sense of what it produces. Human attention does not suddenly expand because the model became more capable. Working memory does not become unlimited because we added an agent. Cognitive psychology has been telling us this for a long time: attention is selective, and working memory can only hold a limited amount of information while we actively process it.  So perhaps the next generation of AI experience should not begin with, “What else can the model generate?” It should begin with something much more human: What do I need to notice? What do I need to understand? What do I need to know before I act? 

That gives us three very simple lenses: See. Think. Act. 

SEE is about priority. What matters now? William James described attention more than a century ago as selective: dealing effectively with one thing requires other things to temporarily recede. That idea becomes much more important when AI can continuously generate another insight, another alert, another explanation, another recommendation. The answer is not simply to show less. Complex work still needs evidence, history, dependencies, and context. The job of the experience is to create hierarchy. Bring what matters into the foreground. Keep supporting information available without forcing it to compete for the same moment of attention. Do not make everything visible. Make what matters visible.

THINK is about connection. How does this fit together? Finding the right information is only the beginning. A summary can make something shorter without making it clearer. An explanation can sound convincing while leaving the structure underneath invisible. So instead of giving someone another paragraph of AI-generated text, help them see the situation itself: driver → evidence → assumption → outcome.What caused the change? What evidence supports that conclusion? What assumption is carrying the recommendation? What remains uncertain? The person should be able to inspect it, question it, and follow the relationship from evidence to consequence. Do not just give people an explanation. Give them something they can think with. Your existing THINK framing makes the same distinction: understanding comes from a representation people can reason with, not simply from receiving an explanation. 

ACT is about judgment. What happens if I do this? Understanding the situation is still not the same as deciding what to do. Gary Klein’s work on naturalistic decision-making found that experienced decision makers can evaluate a plausible action by mentally running it forward, imagining how it might unfold before committing. AI gives us a chance to make that process tangible. Instead of giving someone only Approve and Reject, let them change an assumption. Test another scenario. Add context the system did not know. Ask what happens if demand drops, if a supplier is late, or if service level matters more than inventory cost. And then let the recommendation change with them. Before I commit, let me see what happens next.What-if interaction is not just another feature. It is a tool for judgment.

And this brings us back to where we started. For years, people adapted to the software. Now the software can begin to adapt to the person. Not by putting more intelligence on the screen. Not by filling another dashboard with AI-generated cards. But by knowing what deserves attention, helping people understand how the situation fits together, and allowing them to explore what might happen before they act.

See what matters. Think with the situation. Act with judgment.

That is the opportunity.

Not a smarter dashboard. A better way for humans and intelligence to work together.

Design for Human

With Joule work, people express what they want to accomplish, and Joule Work surfaces the right insights, automates routine work, and coordinates AI agents across systems to achieve it – all in one dynamic workspace. It acts as an engagement layer that spans across SAP products and beyond, and coexists with current experiences provided by pre-defined application UIs.

It represents a new way of interacting with business systems, since it provides:

  • One single place where a user can get tasks done, rather than the traditional app-centric interaction model, where users need to navigate to different applications or even to different products.
  • An intent-driven, situational experience, where users state their intentions in natural language and the system builds on the fly to meet their needs, taking the current business and user context (the current situation and their authorizations) into account: fetching data, triggering AI agents, and visualizing the outcome appropriately.

User-led adoption: Joule Work complements existing application UIs. This lets you and your users adopt AI at your own pace. Users decide where AI can help them. They continue to use application UIs – such as SAP Fiori apps and SAP GUI transactions accessed through the SAP Fiori launchpad - to independently verify agent actions, to extend beyond the agent’s current capabilities, or when familiar screens are simply more comfortable for familiar tasks. Embedded AI features in SAP Fiori apps help encourage users into working the AI way more frequently.

Figure 1: Joule Work experiences: Conversations, Spaces, and Develop. Alt Text: The image shows 3 screenshots, one each for the three experiences. The top of the image has a heading  “Joule Work”, above a row with five attributes: Dynamic, Proactive, Agentic, Intent-based, Omnipresent.

Joule Work provides these experiences:

  • Conversations: this experience allows people to express intent and explore what they want to accomplish through dialogue with Joule Work. It is an AI-powered chat supporting role-based intents, multiple conversation threads, with type-ahead, auto-suggestions and multi-facetted types of responses (text, tables, charts etc.). Joule Work brings together guidance and outcomes from across SAP and third-party systems. Conversations can also act as an entry point to Spaces for more complex workflows.
  • Spaces: provides flexible AI-generated spaces that dynamically adapt content based on user intent and context, for dealing with simple as well as complex tasks and issues. Each space is composed in real time to bring the right data, tools, and context together for a specific goal, allowing people to work in an environment that adapts to their present goal, instead of navigating applications and their pre-defined UIs.​
  • Develop: this experience is provided by Joule Studio, enabling developers to vibe-code, test and deploy AI agents, applications, and automations across SAP and third-party systems. Joule Work provides a convenient entry point to Joule Studio for developers and business users alike, giving them an AI-powered user experience for pro-code and low-code tools.

The Joule Work user experience is available on different kinds of clients (device types), optimized for the device’s capabilities. Three such modalities of Joule Work are available: in the web browser, on mobile devices (tablet, phone) via Joule Work mobile app, and on desktop (laptop, PC) via Joule Work desktop.

Find out more about Joule Work to get a better idea of these experiences:

  • SAP UX Update: The New Joule Work Engagement Layer Experiences
  • Joule Work on sap.com
  • Documentation: Joule Work

This blog post from my series covering public cloud UX innovations gives more information about Joule Work desktop, Joule Work mobile app, as well as SAP Build Work Zone:

  • SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 1: AI, Joule, Mobile, SAP Build Work Zone

Joule Work is planned to become available later this month (October) to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2023 FPS03 and upward, as well as 2025 FPS01 and upward, with SAP-managed Joule and SAP-managed integration of Joule to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition.

 

AI-Assisted UX

The following embedded AI features are now all generally available with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS02, and included in Base, and hence included in your regular license. There’s no additional cost, and no AI Unit usage involved.

AI-Assisted Enterprise Search

You can now use natural language in the search field available at the top of every screen in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, making it even easier to benefit from powerful enterprise search capabilities. With enterprise search, you can find the business objects such as sales orders, deliveries, and invoices directly – as you can see in Figure 2.

Important design principles for us for AI is “human in the loop” and “explainability”. In this case, we display the filters at the top of the search list that AI has identified from the query, so that users can confirm that AI has indeed understood the intent correctly.

Figure 2: AI-assisted enterprise search, showing how you can easily find business data directly using natural language. Alt Text: A short video showing how a user can enter in the search field in the shell header bar “Show me sales orders over 325k usd” and get a corresponding list sales orders. The user than adds the text “open” resulting in a list with fewer results.

Watch the full video:

  • Video:  AI-Assisted Enterprise Search in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition  (0:45 min.)

AI-Assisted Easy Filter

This is another example of interacting via natural language with your application:  in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, you can now easily filter lists using natural language, rather than manually setting the filters for each field in the filter bar. We use SAP Business AI to interpret the query and identify the appropriate filter values. As with AI-assisted enterprise search, we keep the human in the loop and provide explainability: the filter values identified are displayed at the top of the list, so users can get confirmation that their text has been correctly interpreted. Figure 6 shows an example.

Figure 3: AI-assisted easy filter allows you to filter business data using natural language. ALT Text: The Manage Sales Orders – Version 2 app is shown with one text entry field above the list of orders, containing the text “In process orders for customer cbont for delivery this month”. To the right of the text field the “Go” button has the AI icon on the left of the Go text. Below the text entry field identified filters are shown: Overall Status “In Process”, Requested Delivery Date “01.10.2026…31.10.2026, Sold-to Party: CBont Industries”.

From a technical perspective, it is available for SAP Fiori elements list reports – with names along the lines of “Manage <insert your business object here>” apps (for example: Manage Sales Orders)

In addition to filtering, you can use natural language for sorting and grouping.

Sorting and grouping means that you can use natural language to say how you want the result to be sorted, and you can also specify how you want the entries in the table to be grouped.

Figure 4 shows an example with the Manage Sales Orders – Version 2 app, where the user has typed in “Show me sales orders in status open or in process where the net value is >= 50K EUR sorted by net value ascending and grouped by overall status”. Below the line containing the prompt you can see how the app shows the filters that have been identified from the text: overall status (2 values), net value >= 50000, document currency European Euro. The data in the table is sorted and grouped as requested, the first group showing the open orders, the second group those that are in process.

Figure 4: Sorting and grouping with AI-Assisted Easy Filter. Alt-Text: Screenshot showing a list of sales orders with natural language filter request and outcome as described in the above text.

View management: You can save your natural language based filter as a view for the application, just as you have always been able to save views for filters based on defined individual field values in the filter bar.

Watch it in action here, including examples of grouping and view management::

  • Video: AI-Assisted Easy Filter (1:30 min.)

AI-Assisted Easy Filter is available for applications based on SAP Fiori elements, Web Dynpro for ABAP, and Floorplan Manager applications.

AI-Assisted Smart Summarization

Users of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition can use the new smart summarization capability to generate personalizable summaries of object pages based on SAP Fiori elements. You simply select the sections you want to have included in the summary, and let smart summarization create a summary for you. You can edit the result and copy it into your clipboard with just one click, ready to paste into an e-mail, chat or document. Figure 5 shows an example of a summary. If you want to see how to select the sections, watch this:

  • Video: AI-Assisted Smart Summarization (1:00 min.)

Figure 5: AI-Assisted Smart Summarization generates summaries of object pages based on SAP Fiori elements in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2502. ALT Text: A popover is shown with formatted text, the Header saying “Standard Order Summary of 212298”, followed by a brief description and then sections for “Data, Location and Address”, with five bullet points for requested delivery date, document, pricing, and billing dates, and shipping address, “Key Highlights”, showing overall status, overall block status, incompletion status and more.

AI-Assisted Error Explanation

New users who are unfamiliar with the system may find that the short error messages give too little information for them to fully understand the issue, and what to do about it. This is where the AI-Assisted Error Explanation in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition can help: it uses SAP Business AI to summarize information which explains the error and provide a recommendation for how to resolve it. Figure 6 shows an example where a user has entered a Sold-to-Party ID which does not exist in the system.

This feature is available for applications based on SAP Fiori elements.

Figure 6: AI-Assisted Error Explanation. ALT Text: On the left the field “Sold-to Party containing “ABC” is marked red, below that a  popover with an error message “No customer master record exists for sold-to-party AABC”, and in the text line below that the AI icon followed by “Explain link. An arrow leads from this link to a popover, which indicates what happens when you click on this text: you get a popover with an short “Understanding the issue” section and a longer “Resolving the issue” section with a list of actions.

Have a look:

  • Video: AI-Assisted Error Explanation (40 seconds)

List of Supported AI-Assisted SAP Fiori Apps

This SAP note has an Excel file attached that lists all the SAP Fiori apps that support Easy Filter, Smart Summarization, and Easy Fill:

  • SAP Note: 3692870 - Configuration of Base AI-Assisted Features in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Although the note refers to the Public Edition, it does also apply to those Fiori apps listed there that are available in the Private Edition.

Find out more:

To get started with these AI-assisted features, have a look at this great blog post from Jocelyn Dart, as well as the documentation:

  • SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Getting started with Base AI-assisted Features in 2025 FPS2
  • There’s help for your administrator in the SAP Fiori launchpad > Administration guide section Enabling AI-assisted features.
  • And help for your users in the SAP Fiori launchpad > User guide section Using AI-Assisted Features.

Of course, you will want to tell your users all about these new AI-assisted features and encourage them to try them out! A great way to pass on the latest news and tips is via the Manage News app – where you post news for users to see in their Display News tile in their My Home page.

If you haven’t configured this yet, as usual your administrator will find the instructions in the SAP Fiori launchpad > Administration guide section Manage News.

 

Manage News App now with “Must be Read” Feature

News articles containing essential company information can now be designated as required reading. All users must acknowledge that they have read and understood the content.

The main benefits of this feature are:

  • Strengthens accountability: When reading is mandatory, employees can be held accountable for understanding essential information. This practice helps ensure compliance with legal, safety, and policy-related requirements.
  • Ensures consistent knowledge across the organization: All employees receive the same information, minimizing knowledge gaps and miscommunication.
  • Enhances change management : During periods of transition—such as the introduction of new policies or process changes—required reading ensures that all employees understand the reasons behind and the impacts of those changes.

Figure 7 shows what this looks like for a user: a required reading pop-over appears on their screen. The article has also been flagged as “Containing Critical News”.

Figure 7: An example of a news article that is required reading. Alt Text: A screenshot of My Home with a pop-over “Required Reading” that is also highlighted with “Contains Critical News”. The news article has an image at the top, followed by text showing the first part of the article. The “Done” button is greyed out, the “Remind me later” button is visible.

Figure 8 below shows the Manage News app, with the toggles Critical and the new Required Reading one.

Figure 8: The Manage News app has a toggle to mark articles as “Required Reading”. Alt Text: Screenshot of the Manage News app with the toggles set to “Yes”, and some news text in the Description field.

Get an overview of the Manage News app, including the required reading feature:

  • Video: Manage News Application in My Home (1:55 min.)
  • Video: Manage News: Required Reading (1:00 min.)

Fast with SAP Fiori: one-minute videos for end-users

SAP Fiori apps help users work quickly and efficiently – especially when they take advantage of the many time-saving features that are built in. We have found that users are often not aware of some of these features, so to mitigate that, we now provide several one-minute videos for users.

You can have a look at them using this link, which takes you to the landing page displayed in Figure 9:

  • Fast with SAP Fiori – One tip, one minute.

Since we want to help the actual users of the system, we have made them directly accessible via the built-in help within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, as shown in Figure 9 further below.

Figure 9: Fast with SAP Fiori landing page. Alt Text: a screenshot of the web page with two rows of cards: first a card for Additional Languages, followed by ten cards, one for each video, with a thumbnail screenshot, title and brief description.

At the time of writing we provide the ten videos featured in Figure 8, covering the following topics:

  1. Perform Actions on Table Items
    How to use the context menu in a table to trigger relevant actions.
  2. Copy and Paste in Tables
    How to copy whole lines, sections or cells of a table, and how to paste data into tables.
  3. Manage Favorites in My Home
    How to manage your favorite apps in the My Home page: adding apps, grouping them, changing the color as well as removing apps.
  4. Find Keyboard Shortcuts
    How to display the keyboard shortcuts available to you on the section of the screen you are currently using.
  5. Personalize the Table Layout
    How to define and store specific table layouts: hide, add, reorder columns, sort, filter and group entries, and save the layout for reuse.
  6. Adapt the UI (for key users)
    How to adapt the layout of the UI, and also how to change the text arrangement in fields that contain both ID and description: you can choose to show “ID (description)”, “description (ID)”, or only “ID” or only “description”.
  7. Finding Apps
    How to find applications – recent activities, frequently used, or using search.
  8. Saving Filter Values as Views
    How to save specific filter values as reusable views, and how to share them with colleagues if needed.
  9. Adapt your User Settings
    How to change settings such as appearance (light / dark), date format, time zone, decimal format, and how you can personalize search.
  10. Set Default Values
    How to define default values for IDs such as your company code, sales organization etc., so that you don’t have to enter them every time in filters etc.

The videos are in English, but we offer dubbed versions in these languages:

  • Chinese
  • French
  • German
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Portugese
  • Spanish

For those of you who prefer using YouTube, we now have a playlist for all these videos:

  • YouTube Video Playlist: Fast with SAP Fiori: One Tip Per Minute

If you would like to see some additional tips and tricks for users that are not yet covered by the above series, have a look at the video contained in my blog post from 2023. I have listed the timings of these additional tips below:

  • SAP Fiori: Tips & Tricks for Users of SAP S/4HANA
    • 00:00 SAP Fiori launchpad, editing your pages (personalizing) – this is for the pages in launchpad spaces, not for the My Home page, which is covered by Fast with SAP Fiori.
    • 08:21 Search for business objects.
    • 15:10 Help, Quick Tour for the launchpad, and Tutorials.
    • 20:20 Working with applications Quick Tour.
    • 35:10 Navigation between apps via related objects.

The blog post lists the timings of all the tips at the end, many of which are covered by Fast with SAP Fiori.

 

UI Design and Technology News

This last year we have continued investing in our UI design and technology, adding AI capabilities to make it even easier to create new application experiences, as well as providing new features. Some of the highlights are:

  • Skills for Designing SAP Fiori Applications in Figma
  • UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot)
  • UI5 MCP Server enhancements to help migrate to the latest UI5 best practices
  • SAP Fiori Tools:
    • Project Accelerator for ABAP Cloud
    • MCP Server enhancements and Skills for SAP Fiori development
    • Usability improvements
    • Renovations and Performance Improvements
  • Mobile Optimized for Web
  • Mobile SDKs: New and enhanced components for iOS and Android, and for the Mobile development kit (MDK)

These and more are covered in detail in this blog post:

  • SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 9: AI, AI, but not only! UI Design and Technology for Web and Mobile

 

Final words

As you can see, we continue to innovate the user experience of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, especially when it comes to using AI to help users get better outcomes more easily.

Do keep posting your experiences and recommendations yourself in the SAP Community, with the SAP Fiori and/or the User Experience tag! In case you are wondering how to get a list of the most recent blog posts on SAP Fiori and User Experience in our new SAP Community, use these links:
